1	## Speeding up typing
2	
3	**Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** plays the typing in a screen recording faster, so a viewer does not sit through every keystroke. It reads the typing from the recording's cursor file: a run of at least three typed keys, each less than a second after the last. Only the moments are recorded, never which keys.
4	
5	Select one or more clips whose movies have cursor files and choose the item. The sheet has three settings, remembered for next time:
6	
7	| Setting | Default | What it does |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| Rate | ×4 (×2 to ×8) | How much faster the typing plays |
10	| Shortest stretch | 3 s (1 to 30 s) | Typing shorter than this is left alone |
11	| Keep pitch | On | Keeps the sped-up sound at its own pitch (off, it rises like a fast tape) |
12	
13	The sheet says what Apply would do, for example "2 typing stretches sped up ×4, saving 9.3 s.", or "No typing stretch without speech or a shortcut lasts 3 s or more in the selected clips, so nothing would change." Apply makes one undo step, "Speed Up Typing". It works inside an open nest too, and is greyed when a selected clip is not a movie with a cursor file.
14	
15	- **Speech stays at normal speed.** Any part of a stretch where a clip with sound under it has speech, on any track, is left at normal speed. Frame Job finds the speech on this Mac (the same detection Duck by Speech uses) and saves it with the project in the same undo step. While it is still being detected the sheet says "Waiting for speech detection on …" and updates by itself; after five minutes it stops waiting and asks you to close the sheet and try again. On a Mac where speech detection cannot run, it says so and changes nothing.
16	- **Shortcuts stay at normal speed.** A recorded shortcut and the overlay that shows it (its clip on a "Shortcuts" track, or 1.5 s when there is none) are never sped up, so add the overlays first.
17	- **Clean edges.** Each sped stretch keeps 0.3 s at normal speed at both ends.
18	- **Split recordings.** The halves of a recording you split are treated as one: typing across the cut is one stretch.
19	- **Everything stays in step.** Each stretch is sped with [Retime Range](speed.md#retime-a-range) on every unlocked track, so the camera and the microphone stay in sync and everything after moves up. The sound in a sped stretch is sped too.
20	
21	Nothing changes when any stretch cannot be sped (a locked track after it, a transition touching it, a detached pair in it…): the sheet names the stretch and the reason. A clip that plays reversed is refused. Taking a clip with sound past ×12 asks first, as [The ×12 question](speed.md#the-12-question) says.
22	
23	*Agents:* `speed_up_typing` does the same, and takes `rate`, `shortest`, `keep_pitch` and a `from`/`to` range. It answers each sped range and the time saved.

25	## Permissions
26	
27	A screen recording needs macOS's **Screen Recording** permission (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording**). A recording with a microphone, and every voice-over, also needs the **Microphone** permission (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Microphone**). A camera recording needs the **Camera** permission instead of Screen Recording, and a screen recording with **Record the camera too** needs both. Frame Job asks for each one when you press Record, before the countdown begins:
28	
29	- **Screen Recording.** The first press without it shows macOS's prompt, and the panel explains what to do. Once you've turned it on, relaunch Frame Job if macOS asks you to, then press Record again. Every later press without the permission opens System Settings at the right pane.
30	- **Microphone.** Asked only when a microphone is chosen. If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears, and the countdown starts as soon as you allow it. If you denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Microphone pane.
31	- **Input Monitoring.** Asked only with **Record shortcuts** ticked and a display or window as the source (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring**), after Screen Recording and before the camera and the microphone. macOS shows no prompt for it, and Frame Job isn't in that pane's list until you add it, so the first press both asks and opens System Settings at the Input Monitoring pane; the note says "Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring. If Frame Job is not in its list, add it with +." Turn Frame Job on there (add it with **+** if it isn't listed) and press Record again. Every later press without the permission opens the pane again. No relaunch is needed.
32	- **Camera.** Asked only with **Source** set to **Camera**, or with **Record the camera too** ticked (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Camera**), after Screen Recording when there is a screen and before the microphone. If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears; allowing it goes on to the microphone and the countdown, and denying it leaves the panel idle with a note. If you denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Camera pane and the note says so.
33	
34	While a system prompt or System Settings is up, the panel stops floating above other windows, so it doesn't cover them. It floats again on your next press of Record, or when the panel is opened again.
35	
36	If Frame Job was started from a terminal or another app rather than from the Finder or the Dock, macOS applies that app's permissions instead of Frame Job's. In that case the panel's note names the launching process (by its pid) and says to relaunch with `open -a "Frame Job"`, or to grant the permission to that app (the terminal, for a shell launch).
37	
38	## Limits
39	
40	- The panel records displays, single windows, a camera on its own, and a camera beside a display or a window. A camera records at one of its formats at that format's highest frame rate (not at a lower rate within the format's range). The panel lays a camera beside the screen out in one of five layouts, a corner always the bottom-right one; it has no control for another corner, Stacked, Screen Only, scale or inset. The layout's crop centres on the camera's picture, not on the person. There's no keystroke or callout overlay.
41	- When a stretch of a screen recording is left out because its movie can't be read, its camera file stays on disk and is named with its other kept files, but it isn't added to the project. Only that stretch's microphone is.
42	- There's no global shortcut to stop. Use the menu-bar item or the File menu.
43	- While a screen recording runs, the menu-bar item is the only place to pause or resume besides the File menu. If macOS hides the item, for example behind the notch or in a crowded menu bar, **File ▸ Stop Recording** and **File ▸ Pause Recording** still work.
44	- A recording longer than 9:59:59 shows a label wider than the item was sized for.
45	- When a project is already at its track limit, a recording that needs a new track can't be added. The files stay on disk and the note names them.
46	- If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, no display can be shared, so nothing can be recorded until one wakes.
47	- Record shortcuts writes nothing while any app holds secure input, and a typing mark is a time alone: there's no mode that records what you type.
48	- A **Separate** stretch whose cursor file couldn't be written (the screen never reported its start, or the file couldn't be saved) has no pointer at all: it isn't in the movie and there's nothing to draw it from. The landing's note says so, ending "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."
49	
50	See also: [Audio](audio.md) for setting the microphone and system-audio levels, [Export](export.md) for writing the finished edit, and [Menus and shortcuts](menus-and-shortcuts.md).
51	### When the panel comes back
52	
53	A recording that lands cleanly doesn't bring the panel back. Press ⌥⌘N to open it again. The panel returns on its own, with a note, only when it was on screen when the recording began and there's something to say, for example:
54	
55	- the recording was stopped from macOS's indicator, or the display slept or went away, or the camera stopped on its own
56	- the project you chose had closed, so it opened as a new project
57	- a stretch's movie couldn't be read (for example an empty file from a pause right after a resume) and was left out. Its microphone file still lands on the Microphone track where the picture would have been, and the next picture starts after that gap. The note names the left-out file and the files it kept. Only a recording with no readable movie at all fails, and its note names every file.
58	- the files didn't finish writing within 10 s of Stop. The note reads "The recording did not finish writing within 10 s." and names the movie and microphone files kept on disk.
59	- the microphone stopped or failed (the picture still landed)
60	- a resume failed
61	- a file couldn't be placed and was added to the media list only
62	- the recording was saved but couldn't be added. The note reads "The recording was saved at … but could not be added: …" and names every file.
63	
64	## Voice-overs (Microphone Only)
65	
66	To record narration over your edit, choose **Microphone Only** in **Source**:
67	
68	- **System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size** and **Include Frame Job windows** grey out. Their values are kept for next time.
69	- **Rate** stays live, because it sets the rate of a new project. **Microphone** and **Record Into** stay live too.
70	- You must choose a microphone. With **Off**, Record says "Microphone Only records the microphone alone — choose a microphone first."
71	- Only the Microphone permission is checked. Screen Recording isn't needed.
72	
73	The countdown and the menu-bar item work as they do for a screen recording. Unlike a screen recording, **the panel stays up** while a voice-over records. Its controls lock, the meter stays live, the footnote shows ● or ❚❚ and the elapsed time, Record reads **Stop**, and a **Pause** / **Resume** button appears beside it. If you close the panel, the voice-over carries on. Stop it from the menu-bar item or **File ▸ Stop Recording** (⌥⌘N), and use the welcome window's **New Recording…** button to bring the panel back.
74	
75	Each stretch between pauses is its own `.m4a` file. In an open project, every file lands on a **new back track named Microphone**, end to end from the playhead, as one **Add Recording** undo step. It never goes on an existing track. As a new project, the first file is the project (1920×1080 at the chosen rate) and later files follow it on its one track.
76	
77	While a voice-over records, the panel's note shows a refused **Resume** as it happens: the reason appears there and the voice-over stays paused.
78	
79	If the microphone stops on its own (for example, it's unplugged), the voice-over ends there and what was recorded still lands, with a note.

383	/// A source tick `s` of `clip` in container time, when inside its played
384	/// window `[in, in + content_length_in_source)` (CU8's mapping, through S).
385	fn played_at(project: &Project, clip: &Clip, s: Ticks) -> Option<Ticks> {
386	    let (_, source_in) = media_in(clip)?;
387	    let length = project.content_length_in_source(clip);
388	    (source_in <= s && s < source_in.saturating_add(length))
389	        .then(|| clip.start.saturating_add(clip_time(clip, s - source_in)))

392	/// CU-91 (1): `clip`'s typing stretches, clamped to its played window, in
393	/// container time, inside `window`.
394	fn stretches_of(
395	    project: &Project,
396	    clip: &Clip,
397	    track: &CursorTrack,
398	    window: (Ticks, Ticks),
399	) -> Vec<(Ticks, Ticks)> {
400	    let Some((_, source_in)) = media_in(clip) else {
401	        return Vec::new();
402	    };
403	    let source_end = source_in.saturating_add(project.content_length_in_source(clip));
404	    let mut out = Vec::new();
405	    for (first, last, _) in typing_stretches(&track.file().keys.typed.t) {
406	        let (s0, s1) = (us_to_ticks(first).max(source_in), us_to_ticks(last));
407	        let s1 = s1.min(source_end);
408	        if s1 <= s0 {
409	            continue;
410	        }
411	        let at = |s: Ticks| clip.start.saturating_add(clip_time(clip, s - source_in));
412	        let (a, b) = (at(s0).max(window.0), at(s1).min(window.1));
413	        if b > a {
414	            out.push((a, b));
415	        }
416	    }
417	    out
418	}

420	/// CU-91 (2b): every recorded shortcut's overlay span for `clip`, with no
421	/// `[from, to)` filter on the presses.
422	fn overlay_spans(project: &Project, clip: &Clip, track: &CursorTrack) -> Vec<(Ticks, Ticks)> {
423	    let shortcuts: BTreeSet<u32> = project
424	        .tracks
425	        .iter()
426	        .filter(|t| t.name == TRACK_NAME)
427	        .map(|t| t.id)
428	        .collect();
429	    let late = seconds_to_ticks(MOST_LATE);
430	    let fallback = seconds_to_ticks(DEFAULT_DURATION);
431	    let mut out = Vec::new();
432	    for &t in &track.file().keys.shortcut.t {
433	        let Some(p) = played_at(project, clip, us_to_ticks(t)) else {
434	            continue;
435	        };
436	        let before = out.len();
437	        for c in project
438	            .clips
439	            .iter()
440	            .filter(|c| shortcuts.contains(&c.track))
441	        {
442	            let holds = c.start <= p && p < end(c);
443	            let soon = p < c.start && c.start <= p.saturating_add(late);
444	            if holds || soon {
445	                out.push((p.min(c.start), end(c)));
446	            }
447	        }
448	        if out.len() == before {
449	            out.push((p, p.saturating_add(fallback)));
450	        }
451	    }
452	    out
453	}

455	/// `piece` less every span of `cuts`.
456	fn subtract(piece: (Ticks, Ticks), cuts: &[(Ticks, Ticks)]) -> Vec<(Ticks, Ticks)> {
457	    let mut left = vec![piece];
458	    for &(c0, c1) in cuts {
459	        left = left
460	            .into_iter()
461	            .flat_map(|(a, b)| {
462	                if c1 <= a || b <= c0 {
463	                    return vec![(a, b)];
464	                }
465	                [(a, c0.min(b)), (c1.max(a), b)]
466	                    .into_iter()
467	                    .filter(|(x, y)| y > x)
468	                    .collect()
469	            })
470	            .collect();
471	    }
472	    left
473	}

475	/// Pieces sorted and merged where they overlap or touch (CU-91 (3)).
476	fn united(mut pieces: Vec<(Ticks, Ticks)>) -> Vec<(Ticks, Ticks)> {
477	    pieces.sort_unstable();
478	    let mut out: Vec<(Ticks, Ticks)> = Vec::with_capacity(pieces.len());
479	    for (a, b) in pieces {
480	        match out.last_mut() {
481	            Some(last) if a <= last.1 => last.1 = last.1.max(b),
482	            _ => out.push((a, b)),
483	        }
484	    }
485	    out
486	}

527	/// Each run of `t` (µs, in order) whose neighbours are less than `gap`
528	/// apart and which holds at least `min` entries, as (first, last, count).
529	fn runs(t: &[i64], gap: i64, min: usize) -> Vec<(i64, i64, usize)> {
530	    let mut out = Vec::new();
531	    let mut start = 0;
532	    for i in 1..=t.len() {

534	            if i - start >= min {

351	/// note is rebuilt from `[microphoneProblem, resumeProblem]` at every tick
352	/// (`syncMicrophoneNote`, over `liveNote` below), so a microphone
353	/// did-finish landing late cannot wipe it and a retried resume replaces it
354	/// rather than appending a second copy; and `landingNote` takes it as an
355	/// argument, so the landing's note carries it where the first shape — each
356	/// end replacing the label whole — dropped it, and the reveal showed
357	/// nothing. A resume that LANDS clears it: a sentence about a refusal the
358	/// person has since got past would bring the panel back with nothing true
359	/// to say.
360	///
361	/// A Stop while paused (`stopRecording`, `record(_:)`, File ▸ Stop
362	/// Recording) goes to `recorder.stop()` exactly as one while recording
363	/// does — the recorder's `.paused` arm takes the same finishing path with
364	/// the segment's output already closed — and the status item comes down at
365	/// `recordingEnded` as ever. The tick runs through `.paused` (`armTick`):
366	/// the meter poll is a no-op there, the recorder having silenced the bar at
367	/// the pause, and `elapsed` is frozen, so the footnote and the item hold
368	/// still on their own.
369	extension RecorderPanelController {
370	    // MARK: - Pause and resume
371	
372	    /// The status item's Pause Recording, and File ▸ Pause Recording's for
373	    /// the panel's own recording. `.recording` → `.paused`; any
374	    /// other phase beeps — the row was clicked in the moment between a Stop
375	    /// and the item coming down — and so does any throw, `.alreadyPaused`
376	    /// among them (the header).
377	    func pauseRecording() {
378	        guard phase == .recording else {
379	            NSSound.beep()
380	            return
381	        }
382	        do {
383	            try recorder.pause()
384	            phase = .paused
385	        } catch {
386	            NSSound.beep()
387	        }
388	    }
389	
390	    /// The status item's Resume Recording, and File ▸ Resume Recording's.
391	    /// `.paused` → `.recording`, with
392	    /// the refused-resume sentence cleared; any other phase beeps. A throw
393	    /// leaves the phase paused and keeps the recorder's sentence as
394	    /// `resumeProblem`, REPLACING an earlier one, redrawn into the note at
395	    /// once rather than at the tick's next turn (the header).
396	    func resumeRecording() {
397	        guard phase == .paused else {
398	            NSSound.beep()
399	            return
400	        }
401	        do {
402	            try recorder.resume()
403	            resumeProblem = nil
404	            phase = .recording
405	        } catch {
406	            resumeProblem = error.localizedDescription
407	            syncMicrophoneNote()
408	        }
409	    }
410	
411	    /// The live note's two parts, in order: the microphone's sentence, with
412	    /// the fact that the picture is still recording (a silent meter alone
413	    /// reads as a broken recording), then a refused resume's; empty with
414	    /// neither. Pure, so a probe can pin the composition without a recorder.
415	    static func liveNote(microphoneProblem: String?, resumeProblem: String?) -> String {
416	        var sentences: [String] = []
417	        if let microphoneProblem {
418	            sentences.append(
419	                "The microphone stopped: \(microphoneProblem) The picture is still recording.")
420	        }
421	        if let resumeProblem { sentences.append(resumeProblem) }
422	        return sentences.joined(separator: " ")
423	    }
424	
425	    // MARK: - The hidden recording's one door
426	
427	    /// The quit guard's call (`AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate`).
428	    /// While this panel is hidden for its recording `show()` can only beep,
429	    /// and a beep tells a person who paused and forgot nothing — so the
430	    /// status item's menu is opened instead, Pause or Resume and Stop put
431	    /// in front of them (`RecorderStatusItem.openMenu`); the beep is kept
432	    /// for the one case with no item to open. Any other recording — a
433	    /// tool's, which File ▸ Stop Recording ends — shows the panel as before.
434	    func revealControls() {
435	        guard hiddenForRecording else {
436	            show()
437	            return
438	        }
439	        if statusItem?.openMenu() != true { NSSound.beep() }
440	    }
441	
442	    // MARK: - The phases, drawn
443	
444	    /// Draws the phase: the button's title and enabled state, the controls
445	    /// locked while anything is in flight, the countdown numeral, the
446	    /// footnote, the camera preview (CAM-7), and the window refitted to
447	    /// whatever appeared or went.
448	    func syncPhase() {
449	        syncControlsEnabled()
450	        syncPauseButton()
451	        var countdown: String?
452	        switch phase {
453	        case .idle:
454	            recordButton.title = "Record"
455	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
456	        case .countdown(let remaining):
457	            recordButton.title = "Cancel"
458	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
459	            countdown = "\(remaining)"
460	        case .starting:
461	            recordButton.title = "Starting…"
462	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
463	        case .recording, .paused:
464	            recordButton.title = "Stop"
465	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
466	        case .stopping:
467	            recordButton.title = "Stopping…"
468	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
469	        case .landing:
470	            recordButton.title = "Adding…"
471	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
472	        }
473	        recordButton.invalidateIntrinsicContentSize()
474	        countdownLabel.stringValue = countdown ?? ""
475	        countdownLabel.isHidden = countdown == nil
476	        refreshStatusLabel()
477	        syncCameraPreview()
478	        fitWindowToContent()
479	    }
480	
481	    /// The footnote: the folder while idle, the coral dot and the elapsed
482	    /// time while recording, the pause glyph and the frozen time while
483	    /// paused — faint, because the dot's colour means "capturing" — and
484	    /// through `.stopping` whichever of those two it last showed, left
485	    /// UNTOUCHED (R2 review): the phase no longer says whether the Stop
486	    /// came from paused, `elapsed` is frozen at the stop call, and
487	    /// redrawing the arm as recording brought the coral dot back over a
488	    /// finish that captures nothing. The status item keeps its mark the
489	    /// same way (`RecorderStatusItem.freeze`, called by `stopRecording`).
490	    func refreshStatusLabel() {
491	        switch phase {
492	        case .recording:
493	            statusLabel.stringValue = "● " + RecorderStatusItem.label(for: recorder.elapsed)
494	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.meterClip
495	        case .paused:
496	            statusLabel.stringValue =
497	                RecorderStatusItem.pauseGlyph + " " + RecorderStatusItem.label(for: recorder.elapsed)
498	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textFaint
499	        case .stopping:
500	            break
501	        default:
502	            statusLabel.stringValue =
503	                "saved in " + (RecordingFiles.folder().path as NSString).abbreviatingWithTildeInPath
504	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textFaint
505	        }
506	    }
507	}
508	// app/Sources/RecordingLanding+LeftOut.swift — a left-out segment's readable
509	// microphone in the landing (#181 item 2, spec §11 recording: "A left-out
510	// segment's readable microphone lands without its picture").
511	//
512	// A segment the walker left out (`RecordingResult.unreadable`) whose
513	// microphone file read carries it as `micDescriptor`, with `position` its
514	// place among the landed segments; `RecordingResult.stretches` lists the
515	// landed segments and those voices in recording order. Here is what the
516	// landing makes of that list: the PICTURE side as `PictureStretch`es — a
517	// landed segment's media, or a GAP the length of the voice snapped down to
518	// the frame, so the picture track stays empty there and the next picture
519	// starts at the slot's end — and the MICROPHONE side as `Voice`s, one per
520	// stretch, a voice-only one at offset 0 because no picture is there to align
521	// it to. `split` maps a per-stretch answer back to the `Placement`'s
522	// per-segment lists and its per-left-out-segment lists; `remainderStretches`
523	// is `remainderPlacement`'s clip-1 branch over the same list. With no
524	// left-out voice every stretch is a segment and every list is the one it was.
525	//
526	// In its own file because `RecordingLanding+Microphone.swift` stood at 381
527	// lines against the 400-line cap for a new file; `view` and `trimmed` are
528	// the base file's, internal for it.
529	
530	import AppKit
531	
532	extension RecordingLanding {
533	    /// One stretch of the picture track: a landed segment's media, placed
534	    /// by `placeBackToBack`, or a gap of `Ticks` it leaves empty.
535	    enum PictureStretch {
536	        case picture(UInt32)
537	        case gap(Ticks)
538	    }
539	
540	    /// One stretch's microphone: its file when one landed (nil when none),
541	    /// and the offset its clip is placed by — a segment's measured
542	    /// `micOffset`, or 0 for a left-out voice.
543	    struct Voice {
544	        let descriptor: MediaDescriptor?
545	        let offset: Ticks
546	    }
547	
548	    /// One `Voice` per stretch of `result`, in order.
549	    static func voices(of result: RecordingResult) -> [Voice] {
550	        result.stretches.map { stretch in
551	            switch stretch {
552	            case .segment(let k):
553	                return Voice(
554	                    descriptor: result.segments[k].micDescriptor,
555	                    offset: result.segments[k].micOffset)
556	            case .voiceOnly(let i):
557	                return Voice(descriptor: result.unreadable[i].micDescriptor, offset: 0)
558	            }
559	        }
560	    }
561	
562	    /// One `PictureStretch` per stretch of `result`: segment `k`'s picture
563	    /// as `mediaIds[k]` (the ids its `add_media` answered, one per segment),
564	    /// and a left-out voice as a gap of `slotLength`, measured against the
565	    /// container `trial` and `scope` name.
566	    static func pictureStretches(
567	        of result: RecordingResult, mediaIds: [UInt32], in trial: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?
568	    ) throws -> [PictureStretch] {
569	        try result.stretches.map { stretch in
570	            switch stretch {
571	            case .segment(let k):
572	                return .picture(mediaIds[k])
573	            case .voiceOnly(let i):
574	                guard let voice = result.unreadable[i].micDescriptor else { return .gap(0) }
575	                return .gap(try slotLength(voice, in: trial, scope: scope))
576	            }
577	        }
578	    }
579	
580	    /// The slot a voice-only stretch takes on the picture track: the file's
581	    /// length snapped DOWN to the container's frame — the length its clip
582	    /// takes (`SilenceDetector.snapDownToFrame`, the one Swift spelling of
583	    /// that snap, `rc_time_snap_to_frame` over the FFI) — and 0 for a file
584	    /// under a frame, which mints no clip and so takes no time.
585	    static func slotLength(_ voice: MediaDescriptor, in trial: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?) throws
586	        -> Ticks
587	    {
588	        let fps = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas.fps
589	        return max(0, SilenceDetector.snapDownToFrame(voice.duration, fps: fps))
590	    }
591	
592	    /// A per-stretch list, `result.stretches`' order, split into one entry
593	    /// per landed segment and one per left-out segment (nil for a left-out
594	    /// segment with no voice, which has no stretch).
595	    static func split(_ list: [UInt32?], of result: RecordingResult)
596	        -> (segments: [UInt32?], leftOut: [UInt32?])
597	    {
598	        var segments: [UInt32?] = result.segments.map { _ in nil }
599	        var leftOut: [UInt32?] = result.unreadable.map { _ in nil }
600	        for (stretch, id) in zip(result.stretches, list) {
601	            switch stretch {
602	            case .segment(let k): segments[k] = id
603	            case .voiceOnly(let i): leftOut[i] = id
604	            }
605	        }
606	        return (segments, leftOut)
607	    }
608	
609	    /// `remainderPlacement`'s clip-1 branch over the stretches: a left-out
610	    /// voice BEFORE clip 1 — the document at 0 — gets no start (media only)
611	    /// and `leadingVoiceNote`; clip 1 is its own stretch; everything after
612	    /// it goes on clip 1's track from clip 1's end by `placeBackToBack`, a
613	    /// voice's gap included, a refusal thrown by name (no two-try rule on a
614	    /// fresh document's one track). Answers one start and one picture clip
615	    /// id per stretch, for `addMicrophones` and `split`.
616	    static func remainderStretches(
617	        _ result: RecordingResult, after first: ClipSnapshot, mediaIds: [UInt32],
618	        firstPath: String, scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp],
619	        notes: inout [String]
620	    ) throws -> (starts: [Ticks?], clips: [UInt32?]) {
621	        let stretches = result.stretches
622	        let lead = stretches.firstIndex(of: .segment(0)) ?? 0
623	        var starts: [Ticks?] = stretches.map { _ in nil }
624	        var clips: [UInt32?] = stretches.map { _ in nil }
625	        for case .voiceOnly(let i) in stretches[..<lead] {
626	            if let mic = result.unreadable[i].micDescriptor {
627	                notes.append(leadingVoiceNote(mic.path, before: firstPath))
628	            }
629	        }
630	        starts[lead] = first.start
631	        clips[lead] = first.id
632	        let rest = Array(
633	            try pictureStretches(of: result, mediaIds: mediaIds, in: trial, scope: scope)[
634	                (lead + 1)...])
635	        guard !rest.isEmpty else { return (starts, clips) }
636	        guard
637	            let placed = try placeBackToBack(
638	                rest, on: first.track, from: first.end, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops,
639	                notes: &notes)
640	        else {
641	            throw ReelCoreError(
642	                message: "The recording's later segments could not be placed after its first.")
643	        }
644	        for (k, landed) in placed.enumerated() {
645	            starts[lead + 1 + k] = landed.at
646	            clips[lead + 1 + k] = landed.clip?.id
647	        }
648	        return (starts, clips)
649	    }
650	
651	    /// The sentence for a left-out voice recorded BEFORE a new project's
652	    /// first segment, which is the document at 0: there is no timeline
653	    /// before it, so the voice lands as media only.
654	    static func leadingVoiceNote(_ path: String, before first: String) -> String {
655	        "\(path) was added to the media list without a clip: it was recorded before \(first), "
656	            + "which starts the new project at 0."
657	    }
658	}
659	// app/Sources/RecordingLanding+Placing.swift — one clip on the grid, asked
660	// of the core (road map 3, R2's toll): a PURE MOVE out of
661	// `RecordingLanding.swift` at the 400-line cap, holding `placeBackToBack`
662	// (a sequence of clips, each at the previous END as read back), `placeClip`
663	// (one `add_clip`, read back and stepped a frame up when the core snapped
664	// it under its floor — the inexact-rate rule the base file's header
665	// argues), `tooShortNote` (a file with no WHOLE frame inside it),
666	// `mediaEntry` and `milliseconds`. Every "what will the core snap this to"
667	// here is put to the core over the FFI — `ReelTime.snapToFrame` is
668	// `rc_time_snap_to_frame` — or read off a purely-applied result; nothing
669	// re-derives a frame in Swift, which is what makes the answers exact at
670	// 24981/1000 as at 30. Internal, not private, because the microphone file
671	// calls all of them and `private` does not cross a file.
672	
673	import AppKit
674	
675	extension RecordingLanding {
676	    /// `media` as touching clips on `track`: the first at `at`, each later
677	    /// one at the previous clip's END as read off the trial after its
678	    /// `add_clip` — never computed here, because a sum over descriptor
679	    /// durations would be off-grid. Each is placed by `placeClip`, which
680	    /// reads the landed clip back and steps a frame up when the core snapped
681	    /// it under the previous end (an inexact rate; the header says why), so
682	    /// two clips meet at one tick or leave a sub-frame gap and never overlap
683	    /// (`core/src/transition.rs`: `overlap_of` answers none at zero length).
684	    /// A picture too short for a frame — the core's `whole_media_length`
685	    /// answers an `Err` for it, and that `Err` used to take the whole list
686	    /// down — lands as media alone, with its sentence in `notes`, and
687	    /// the sequence carries on from the same point. nil when any `add_clip`
688	    /// refuses — the caller decides what a refusal means — and a throw is
689	    /// the core's own sentence. A `.gap` (a left-out segment's voice, #181
690	    /// item 2) places nothing: its `Landed` has no clip and starts where the
691	    /// sequence had reached, and the next picture starts the gap's length
692	    /// later. Answers one `Landed` per stretch, in order.
693	    static func placeBackToBack(
694	        _ stretches: [PictureStretch], on track: UInt32, from at: Ticks, scope: UInt32?,
695	        to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp], notes: inout [String]
696	    ) throws -> [Landed]? {
697	        var placed: [Landed] = []
698	        var at = at
699	        for stretch in stretches {
700	            let id: UInt32
701	            switch stretch {
702	            case .gap(let length):
703	                placed.append(Landed(clip: nil, at: at))
704	                at += length
705	                continue
706	            case .picture(let media):
707	                id = media
708	            }
709	            let file = try mediaEntry(id, in: trial, scope: scope)
710	            let fps = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas.fps
711	            if let note = tooShortNote(file, at: fps) {
712	                notes.append(note)
713	                placed.append(Landed(clip: nil, at: at))
714	                continue
715	            }
716	            guard
717	                let landed = try placeClip(
718	                    id, on: track, at: at, notBelow: at, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops)
719	            else { return nil }
720	            placed.append(Landed(clip: landed, at: landed.start))
721	            at = landed.end
722	        }
723	        return placed
724	    }
725	
726	    /// `add_clip` of `media` on `track` at `at`, applied purely and READ
727	    /// BACK, and never landed below `floor` (≤ `at`): the core snaps the
728	    /// start to the nearest frame, and at an inexact canvas rate the
729	    /// nearest frame to a clip's end can be UNDER it — the end is a sum of
730	    /// two grid points, which is not one — so a landing under the floor is
731	    /// discarded whole and the add is made again at `floor` plus a frame,
732	    /// whose nearest frame is at or above the floor and within a frame of
733	    /// it. What comes back therefore satisfies `floor ≤ start ≤ at + frame`:
734	    /// touching, or a sub-frame gap at an inexact rate, never an overlap
735	    /// (which the rule would accept and dress as a transition). A landing
736	    /// outside that band after the second try is a throw, not a guess. nil
737	    /// is the core's refusal — an overlap the rule will not accept — and
738	    /// the op is appended and the trial advanced only for the clip returned.
739	/// a paused recording is not — so it is drawn in whatever the menu bar
740	/// draws its text in, light or dark.
741	///
742	/// **While shortcuts record** (road map creator-jobs CU6, spec §11 CU-61; the
743	/// owner: a keyboard mark plus a menu row) — `keys`, from the recorder's
744	/// `recordsKeys` at construction — the title carries `keysGlyph` after the
745	/// dot or the pause glyph, in the menu bar's own colour, and the menu's first
746	/// row is a disabled `keysRow` and a separator, paused or not. The length is
747	/// fixed per item for the marks it shows (`itemLength(keys:)`), so an item
748	/// without shortcuts keeps the one length, title and menu it always had.
749	final class RecorderStatusItem: NSObject {
750	    /// Two heavy vertical bars (U+275A). The panel's footnote spells a pause
751	    /// with the same glyph, from here, so the two never drift apart.
752	    static let pauseGlyph = "❚❚"
753	    /// The keyboard (U+2328) with the text presentation selector, so the menu bar draws it in
754	    /// its own ink and never as an emoji (CU-61).
755	    static let keysGlyph = "⌨\u{FE0E}"
756	    /// The menu's first, disabled row while shortcuts record (CU-61).
757	    static let keysRow = "Recording keyboard shortcuts"
758	    /// The longest time the item is sized for (the type doc).
759	    static let widestElapsed: TimeInterval = 35_999
760	    /// Room each side of the title inside the item.
761	    static let titleInset: CGFloat = 6
762	    /// The item's one length: the wider of the two marks' titles at
763	    /// `widestElapsed`, rounded up, plus the insets (the type doc).
764	    static let itemLength: CGFloat = RecorderStatusItem.itemLength(keys: false)
765	
766	    /// The length for an item that shows the keyboard mark or not: the wider of the two marks'
767	    /// titles at `widestElapsed`, rounded up, plus the insets (CU-61).
768	    static func itemLength(keys: Bool) -> CGFloat {
769	        [false, true].map { paused in
770	            ceil(
771	                RecorderStatusItem.title(elapsed: widestElapsed, paused: paused, keys: keys)
772	                    .size().width)
773	                + 2 * titleInset
774	        }.reduce(0, max)
775	    }
776	
777	    /// Whether this item shows the keyboard mark and row: the recording records shortcuts.
778	    let keys: Bool
779	    private let onPause: () -> Void

29	/// The recorder panel from the recording's END to the note that says where
30	/// it went (road map 3, R1c) — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s fourth
31	/// file, cut out of `+Recording.swift` along the line `recordingEnded`
32	/// draws when the R1 review's fixes took that file past the 400-line cap:
33	/// everything before the session's `onFinish` fires stays there, everything
34	/// after it is here.
35	///
36	/// **One door for a finished recording.** The session's `onFinish` — called
37	/// exactly once whoever ended the recording: the panel's Stop, the status
38	/// item's, the system indicator's, a display that slept, a failure — arrives
39	/// at `recordingEnded`, which tears the recording chrome down (the tick, the
40	/// status item, and the `hiddenForRecording` flag that made `show()` beep —
41	/// clearing it, and showing NOTHING) and then lands. A DOCUMENT target
42	/// commits the placement through the document's
43	/// own door (`performGroupedEdit`, then `generateCaches`, the selection, and
44	/// the editor told through `viewStateDidChange`); a NEW PROJECT is
45	/// `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`, which does everything. A document
46	/// mid-drag is not committed over the gesture's base handle: the landing is
47	/// retried from a half-second timer until the drag ends, bounded at forty
48	/// tries — **20 s, kept** (lane C's flag, closed by reading): a landing that
49	/// waited for ever would hold the file's note back for ever, and the note
50	/// after the bound names the file, which is on disk either way — and on
51	/// either failure the note names the FILE, which is on disk whatever went
52	/// wrong after it. That timer stays in the DEFAULT run-loop mode on
53	/// purpose, unlike the countdown and the tick: a drag runs the loop in
54	/// tracking mode, so the retry fires when the drag ENDS, which is the
55	/// moment it is for.
56	///
57	/// **The commit is checked by its handle** (R1 review). `performGroupedEdit`
58	/// answers nothing: a refusal beeps or puts up the core's sentence on the
59	/// document's window and returns, and the panel — which cannot see either
60	/// — used to report "added" over a project with nothing in it. The
61	/// document's `project` handle changes ONLY on success (`applyEdit`'s three
62	/// outcomes), so `land` reads it before the commit and compares after, and
63	/// an unchanged handle is a failed landing with the file's path in the
64	/// note. The trial in `RecordingLanding.placement` sees everything the
65	/// commit will, so the arm is reached only by a race the trial cannot see —
66	/// an edit landing between the two on the same run-loop turn — and it is
67	/// there because the alternative is a note that lies.
68	///
69	/// **The note says six things, in order**, through `landingNote`, a pure
70	/// function so a probe can pin every combination without a landing: how the
71	/// recording ended when it was not this panel's own Stop (`.stopped` is the
72	/// status item's Stop too; `.userStopped` is the SYSTEM's indicator, and the
73	/// sentence names it so, now that Frame Job's own item is a menu-bar item as
74	/// well); that the document the person CHOSE had closed, when the choice
75	/// was a document and the landing opened a new project (R1 review — the
76	/// fallback is exact, and a person who chose "Untitled 2" should not have
77	/// to work out why a new window appeared instead); the segments left out
78	/// because their movie would not probe (`unreadableNote`, #97), each naming
79	/// the files it kept; the microphone's
80	/// problem, when the recording is a `.success` whose `micProblem` is set —
81	/// a success, not an error, so the picture lands first and the sentence
82	/// follows it; a resume the recorder refused (`resumeProblem`, STATE on the
83	/// panel and never text read back off the label — the R2 review's defect:
84	/// each end replaced the label whole, so after a refused resume and a clean
85	/// Stop the note was empty and the reveal showed nothing, the opposite of
86	/// what `+Pause.swift` promised); and the placement's own notes, one per
87	/// file the landing could not place. `failedToLand` names every file
88	/// through `filesClause` and carries the unreadable segments', the
89	/// microphone's and the resume's sentences too.
90	///
91	/// **The panel comes back ONLY with something to say** (decision 7, R2c).
92	/// It ordered out at `recordingDidStart` whatever the source, and each of
93	/// the three ends — `landed`, `failedToLand`, the failure arm of
94	/// `recordingEnded` — finishes with `revealIfNoted()`, AFTER its note is
95	/// set: the panel is ordered front when it was on screen as the recording
96	/// began (`showWhenLanded`) and the note is non-empty, and `showWhenLanded`
97	/// is cleared either way. A clean recording lands in its document or opens
98	/// its project and the panel stays away; ⌥⌘N shows it again. The reveal
99	/// belongs to the END and not to `recordingEnded`, because the deferred
100	/// landing's retries can put twenty seconds between the two, and a panel
101	/// shown with "Adding…" and no note yet is the dialog the user asked to be
102	/// rid of.
103	extension RecorderPanelController {
104	    static let landingRetryInterval: TimeInterval = 0.5
105	    static let landingRetryLimit = 40
106	    static let destinationClosedSentence =
107	        "The document you chose was closed, so the recording opened as a new project."
108	
109	    // MARK: - The end, and the landing
110	
111	    func recordingEnded(_ outcome: Result<RecordingResult, Error>) {
112	        disarmTick()
113	        statusItem?.remove()
114	        statusItem = nil
115	        launched = false
116	        hiddenForRecording = false
117	        switch outcome {
118	        case .failure(let error):
119	            phase = .idle
120	            setNote(
121	                [error.localizedDescription, resumeProblem].compactMap { $0 }
122	                    .joined(separator: " "))
123	            revealIfNoted()
124	        case .success(let result):
125	            phase = .landing
126	            landingAttempts = 0
127	            land(result)
128	        }
129	    }
130	
131	    func land(_ result: RecordingResult) {
132	        switch RecordingLanding.resolve(result.choice.destination) {
133	        case .document(let document):
134	            guard !document.isLiveEditing else {
135	                deferLanding(result)
136	                return
137	            }
138	            do {
139	                let placement = try RecordingLanding.placement(result, in: document, place: true)
140	                let before = document.project
141	                document.performGroupedEdit(RecordingLanding.actionName, placement.ops)
142	                // The handle changes only on success (the type doc).
143	                guard document.project !== before else {
144	                    failedToLand(
145	                        result,
146	                        ReelCoreError(
147	                            message: "the project refused the placement and nothing was added"))
148	                    return
149	                }
150	                document.generateCaches()
151	                // Every segment's clip, microphone clips included (R2b); a
152	                // segment that minted none is a nil entry, and its sentence
153	                // is in `placement.notes`.
154	                document.selection = Set(
155	                    (placement.clipIds + placement.micClipIds + placement.leftOutMicClipIds
156	                        + placement.cameraClipIds)
157	                        .compactMap { $0 })
158	                Self.editor(of: document)?.viewStateDidChange()
159	                landed(result, asNewProject: false, notes: placement.notes)
160	                RecordingCutout.apply(result, in: document)  // CO-81: its own step, first
161	                RecordingEnhance.follow(result, in: document)  // AU-68: after the commit
162	                RecordingPolish.follow(result, in: document)  // CU-100: after it, its own steps
163	            } catch {
164	                failedToLand(result, error)
165	            }
166	        case .newProject:
167	            do {
168	                let (opened, notes) = try ProjectDocument.untitled(around: result)
169	                landed(result, asNewProject: true, notes: notes)
170	                RecordingCutout.apply(result, in: opened)  // CO-81: its own step, first
171	                RecordingEnhance.follow(result, in: opened)  // AU-68: after the commit
172	                RecordingPolish.follow(result, in: opened)  // CU-100: after it, its own steps
173	            } catch {
174	                failedToLand(result, error)
175	            }
176	        }
177	    }
178	
179	    /// A drag is in progress: try again when it has had half a second to
180	    /// end, up to the limit — a landing over the gesture's base handle would
181	    /// be undone by the gesture's own end.
182	    private func deferLanding(_ result: RecordingResult) {
183	        landingAttempts += 1
184	        guard landingAttempts <= Self.landingRetryLimit else {
185	            let waited = Int(Double(Self.landingRetryLimit) * Self.landingRetryInterval)
186	            failedToLand(
187	                result,
188	                ReelCoreError(message: "A drag was still in progress after \(waited) s."))
189	            return
190	        }
191	        landingTimer?.invalidate()
192	        landingTimer = Timer.scheduledTimer(
193	            withTimeInterval: Self.landingRetryInterval, repeats: false
194	        ) { [weak self] _ in
195	            self?.landingTimer = nil
196	            self?.land(result)
197	        }
198	    }
199	
200	    /// Back to idle; the note is `landingNote`'s, over the placement's own
201	    /// notes — the unreadable segments' sentences followed by what became of
202	    /// their readable voices (#181 item 2), said only here, on a landing
203	    /// that succeeded — led by every segment's camera sentences beside the
204	    /// screen (`cameraSegmentsNote`, spec §11 CAM-10 (8)) — and the reveal
205	    /// last.
206	    private func landed(_ result: RecordingResult, asNewProject: Bool, notes placed: [String]) {
207	        phase = .idle
208	        rebuildDestinations()
209	        // Then every segment's cursor problem (spec §11 CU-18).
210	        let notes = [result.cameraSegmentsNote, result.cursorSegmentsNote].compactMap { $0 } + placed
211	        let leftOut = [result.unreadableNote, result.leftOutVoiceNote].compactMap { $0 }
212	        setNote(
213	            Self.landingNote(
214	                stoppedBy: result.stoppedBy, chosen: result.choice.destination,
215	                landedAsNewProject: asNewProject, micProblem: result.micProblem,
216	                resumeProblem: resumeProblem, notes: notes,
217	                unreadable: leftOut.isEmpty ? nil : leftOut.joined(separator: " "),
218	                camera: result.camera, cameraBeside: result.camera != nil && !result.isCamera))
219	        revealIfNoted()
220	    }
221	
222	    /// The files are on disk whatever went wrong after them, so the note
223	    /// names every one (`filesClause`: each segment's movie, and the
224	    /// microphone files that landed) — then what became of an unreadable
225	    /// segment, the microphone, the camera (its `problem` and warm-up `note`,
226	    /// spec §11 CAM-5, then each segment's camera sentences beside the
227	    /// screen, CAM-10 (8)) and a refused resume, when the result or the panel
228	    /// carries those sentences — and the reveal last.
229	    private func failedToLand(_ result: RecordingResult, _ error: any Error) {
230	        phase = .idle
231	        var note =
232	            "The recording was saved at \(result.filesClause) but could not be added: "
233	            + error.localizedDescription
234	        for sentence in [
235	            result.unreadableNote, result.micProblem, result.camera?.problem, result.camera?.note,
236	            result.cameraSegmentsNote, result.cursorSegmentsNote, resumeProblem,
237	        ].compactMap({ $0 })
238	        {
239	            note += " " + sentence
240	        }
241	        setNote(note)
242	        revealIfNoted()
243	    }
244	
245	    /// The panel back on screen after a landing, ONLY when it was on screen
246	    /// as the recording began and the note has something in it (the type
247	    /// doc). Called LAST by each of the three ends, after the note is set —
248	    /// which is the whole point — and reached after the deferred landing's
249	    /// retries as well, since nothing before it clears `showWhenLanded`.
250	    /// Cleared either way, so a later `show()` of the person's own is not
251	    /// mistaken for this one. Internal so a probe can drive both ways.
252	    func revealIfNoted() {
253	        if showWhenLanded, !noteLabel.stringValue.isEmpty { window?.orderFront(nil) }
254	        showWhenLanded = false
255	    }
256	
257	    /// The landing's note (the type doc): the stop's sentence unless the
258	    /// stop was this panel's own; the closed-document sentence when a chosen
259	    /// document was gone by the time the recording ended; the unreadable
260	    /// segments' sentences; the microphone's problem; a refused resume's
261	    /// sentence; then the placement's notes. Empty for the ordinary case, so
262	    /// `setNote` hides the label. The R2 arguments, #97's `unreadable` and
263	    /// CR1c's `camera` are LAST and default, so the probe's R1 rows read as
264	    /// they did. A CAMERA result (spec §11 CAM-5) says its own stop — the
265	    /// camera's `problem`, else that it stopped on its own — in place of the
266	    /// display's, and its warm-up `note` follows the microphone's problem.
267	    /// A camera BESIDE the screen (`cameraBeside`, spec §11 CAM-10 (8)) is
268	    /// not the recording's stop: the display's sentence stays, and the
269	    /// camera's `problem` follows the microphone's problem, before its note.
270	    static func landingNote(
271	        stoppedBy: StopReason, chosen: RecordingDestination, landedAsNewProject: Bool,
272	        micProblem: String?, resumeProblem: String? = nil, notes: [String] = [],
273	        unreadable: String? = nil, camera: RecordingCamera? = nil, cameraBeside: Bool = false
274	    ) -> String {
275	        var sentences: [String] = []
276	        switch stoppedBy {
277	        case .stopped:
278	            break
279	        case .userStopped:
280	            sentences.append(
281	                "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added.")
282	        case .systemStopped:
283	            if let camera, !cameraBeside {
284	                sentences.append(
285	                    (camera.problem ?? "The camera stopped on its own.")
286	                        + " What was captured was added.")
287	            } else {
288	                sentences.append(
289	                    "The system stopped the recording (the display slept or went away); "
290	                        + "what was captured was added.")
291	            }
292	        }
293	        if case .document = chosen, landedAsNewProject {
294	            sentences.append(destinationClosedSentence)
295	        }
296	        if let unreadable { sentences.append(unreadable) }
297	        if let micProblem { sentences.append(micProblem) }
298	        if cameraBeside, let problem = camera?.problem { sentences.append(problem) }
299	        if let note = camera?.note { sentences.append(note) }
300	        if let resumeProblem { sentences.append(resumeProblem) }
301	        sentences.append(contentsOf: notes)
302	        return sentences.joined(separator: " ")
303	    }
304	
305	    /// `AgentServer.editor(_:)`'s lookup; nil for a windowless document.
306	    static func editor(of document: ProjectDocument) -> EditorViewController? {
307	        document.windowControllers
308	            .compactMap { $0.contentViewController as? EditorViewController }
309	            .first
310	    }
311	}

314	/// Pause and resume from the panel's side, the one door into a hidden
315	/// recording's controls, and the phases drawn (road map 3, R2c) —
316	/// `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s sixth file, NEW rather than cut for its
317	/// first two members: they are the whole of what the panel adds for a pause,
318	/// and `+Recording.swift` and the base file were both within a dozen lines
319	/// of the 400-line cap when R2 began. `syncPhase` and `refreshStatusLabel`
320	/// then MOVED here from the base file when the R2 review's fixes took it
321	/// over the cap — the base file's toll, paid along the line the footnote
322	/// draws: its `.paused` and `.stopping` arms are what the pause added, and
323	/// `syncPhase` is its one caller besides the tick.
324	///
325	/// **Neither pause member is reachable from the panel's own controls** but
326	/// in a voice-over, whose panel stays up with a Pause / Resume button
327	/// (`+VoiceOver.swift`). The panel is off screen for every other recording
328	/// (decision 7), so Pause Recording
329	/// and Resume Recording are rows of the status item's menu, which calls
330	/// these through the closures `recordingDidStart` hands it, and File ▸
331	/// Pause/Resume Recording (`AppDelegate+Recording.swift`), the second door,
332	/// which calls them for the panel's own recording (#98). The panel's
333	/// phase — `.recording ⇄ .paused` — follows the recorder's own `pause()` /
334	/// `resume()` (`ScreenRecorder+Pause.swift`), which are synchronous and
335	/// throw. The phase moves only AFTER the call returns
336	/// without throwing, so the panel never claims a state the recorder
337	/// refused: a pause that could not close the segment's file leaves the
338	/// recorder `.recording` and the panel with it, and a resume whose output
339	/// could not be added leaves both `.paused`.
340	///
341	/// **The two refusals are answered differently, on purpose.** A refused
342	/// pause BEEPS: the recorder is still recording, nothing was lost, and the
343	/// panel is hidden, so a note there would be read by nobody until the
344	/// landing, by which time it would be stale. A refused resume keeps the
345	/// recorder's sentence as `resumeProblem` and stays paused: the stream still
346	/// captures but no file is taking it, so what the person does next — try
347	/// again, or stop and land what was recorded — depends on the sentence, and
348	/// the landing's reveal (`revealIfNoted`, `+Landing.swift`) brings the
349	/// panel back with that sentence in its note when they stop. The sentence
350	/// is STATE and never text read back off the label (R2 review): the live
351	/// note is rebuilt from `[microphoneProblem, resumeProblem]` at every tick
352	/// (`syncMicrophoneNote`, over `liveNote` below), so a microphone
353	/// did-finish landing late cannot wipe it and a retried resume replaces it
354	/// rather than appending a second copy; and `landingNote` takes it as an
355	/// argument, so the landing's note carries it where the first shape — each
356	/// end replacing the label whole — dropped it, and the reveal showed
357	/// nothing. A resume that LANDS clears it: a sentence about a refusal the
358	/// person has since got past would bring the panel back with nothing true
359	/// to say.
360	///
361	/// A Stop while paused (`stopRecording`, `record(_:)`, File ▸ Stop
362	/// Recording) goes to `recorder.stop()` exactly as one while recording
363	/// does — the recorder's `.paused` arm takes the same finishing path with
364	/// the segment's output already closed — and the status item comes down at
365	/// `recordingEnded` as ever. The tick runs through `.paused` (`armTick`):
366	/// the meter poll is a no-op there, the recorder having silenced the bar at
367	/// the pause, and `elapsed` is frozen, so the footnote and the item hold
368	/// still on their own.
369	extension RecorderPanelController {
370	    // MARK: - Pause and resume
371	
372	    /// The status item's Pause Recording, and File ▸ Pause Recording's for
373	    /// the panel's own recording. `.recording` → `.paused`; any
374	    /// other phase beeps — the row was clicked in the moment between a Stop
375	    /// and the item coming down — and so does any throw, `.alreadyPaused`
376	    /// among them (the header).
377	    func pauseRecording() {
378	        guard phase == .recording else {
379	            NSSound.beep()
380	            return
381	        }
382	        do {
383	            try recorder.pause()
384	            phase = .paused
385	        } catch {
386	            NSSound.beep()
387	        }
388	    }
389	
390	    /// The status item's Resume Recording, and File ▸ Resume Recording's.
391	    /// `.paused` → `.recording`, with
392	    /// the refused-resume sentence cleared; any other phase beeps. A throw
393	    /// leaves the phase paused and keeps the recorder's sentence as
394	    /// `resumeProblem`, REPLACING an earlier one, redrawn into the note at
395	    /// once rather than at the tick's next turn (the header).
396	    func resumeRecording() {
397	        guard phase == .paused else {
398	            NSSound.beep()
399	            return
400	        }
401	        do {
402	            try recorder.resume()
403	            resumeProblem = nil
404	            phase = .recording
405	        } catch {
406	            resumeProblem = error.localizedDescription
407	            syncMicrophoneNote()
408	        }
409	    }
410	
411	    /// The live note's two parts, in order: the microphone's sentence, with
412	    /// the fact that the picture is still recording (a silent meter alone
413	    /// reads as a broken recording), then a refused resume's; empty with
414	    /// neither. Pure, so a probe can pin the composition without a recorder.
415	    static func liveNote(microphoneProblem: String?, resumeProblem: String?) -> String {
416	        var sentences: [String] = []
417	        if let microphoneProblem {
418	            sentences.append(
419	                "The microphone stopped: \(microphoneProblem) The picture is still recording.")
420	        }
421	        if let resumeProblem { sentences.append(resumeProblem) }
422	        return sentences.joined(separator: " ")
423	    }
424	
425	    // MARK: - The hidden recording's one door
426	
427	    /// The quit guard's call (`AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate`).
428	    /// While this panel is hidden for its recording `show()` can only beep,
429	    /// and a beep tells a person who paused and forgot nothing — so the
430	    /// status item's menu is opened instead, Pause or Resume and Stop put
431	    /// in front of them (`RecorderStatusItem.openMenu`); the beep is kept
432	    /// for the one case with no item to open. Any other recording — a
433	    /// tool's, which File ▸ Stop Recording ends — shows the panel as before.
434	    func revealControls() {
435	        guard hiddenForRecording else {
436	            show()
437	            return
438	        }
439	        if statusItem?.openMenu() != true { NSSound.beep() }
440	    }
441	
442	    // MARK: - The phases, drawn
443	
444	    /// Draws the phase: the button's title and enabled state, the controls
445	    /// locked while anything is in flight, the countdown numeral, the
446	    /// footnote, the camera preview (CAM-7), and the window refitted to
447	    /// whatever appeared or went.
448	    func syncPhase() {
449	        syncControlsEnabled()
450	        syncPauseButton()
451	        var countdown: String?
452	        switch phase {
453	        case .idle:
454	            recordButton.title = "Record"
455	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
456	        case .countdown(let remaining):
457	            recordButton.title = "Cancel"
458	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
459	            countdown = "\(remaining)"
460	        case .starting:
461	            recordButton.title = "Starting…"
462	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
463	        case .recording, .paused:
464	            recordButton.title = "Stop"
465	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
466	        case .stopping:
467	            recordButton.title = "Stopping…"
468	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
469	        case .landing:
470	            recordButton.title = "Adding…"
471	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
472	        }
473	        recordButton.invalidateIntrinsicContentSize()
474	        countdownLabel.stringValue = countdown ?? ""
475	        countdownLabel.isHidden = countdown == nil
476	        refreshStatusLabel()
477	        syncCameraPreview()
478	        fitWindowToContent()
479	    }
480	
481	    /// The footnote: the folder while idle, the coral dot and the elapsed
482	    /// time while recording, the pause glyph and the frozen time while
483	    /// paused — faint, because the dot's colour means "capturing" — and
484	    /// through `.stopping` whichever of those two it last showed, left
485	    /// UNTOUCHED (R2 review): the phase no longer says whether the Stop
486	    /// came from paused, `elapsed` is frozen at the stop call, and
487	    /// redrawing the arm as recording brought the coral dot back over a
488	    /// finish that captures nothing. The status item keeps its mark the
489	    /// same way (`RecorderStatusItem.freeze`, called by `stopRecording`).
490	    func refreshStatusLabel() {
491	        switch phase {
492	        case .recording:
493	            statusLabel.stringValue = "● " + RecorderStatusItem.label(for: recorder.elapsed)
494	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.meterClip
495	        case .paused:
496	            statusLabel.stringValue =
497	                RecorderStatusItem.pauseGlyph + " " + RecorderStatusItem.label(for: recorder.elapsed)
498	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textFaint
499	        case .stopping:
500	            break
501	        default:
502	            statusLabel.stringValue =
503	                "saved in " + (RecordingFiles.folder().path as NSString).abbreviatingWithTildeInPath
504	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textFaint
505	        }
506	    }

508	// app/Sources/RecordingLanding+LeftOut.swift — a left-out segment's readable
509	// microphone in the landing (#181 item 2, spec §11 recording: "A left-out
510	// segment's readable microphone lands without its picture").
511	//
512	// A segment the walker left out (`RecordingResult.unreadable`) whose
513	// microphone file read carries it as `micDescriptor`, with `position` its
514	// place among the landed segments; `RecordingResult.stretches` lists the
515	// landed segments and those voices in recording order. Here is what the
516	// landing makes of that list: the PICTURE side as `PictureStretch`es — a
517	// landed segment's media, or a GAP the length of the voice snapped down to
518	// the frame, so the picture track stays empty there and the next picture
519	// starts at the slot's end — and the MICROPHONE side as `Voice`s, one per
520	// stretch, a voice-only one at offset 0 because no picture is there to align
521	// it to. `split` maps a per-stretch answer back to the `Placement`'s
522	// per-segment lists and its per-left-out-segment lists; `remainderStretches`
523	// is `remainderPlacement`'s clip-1 branch over the same list. With no
524	// left-out voice every stretch is a segment and every list is the one it was.
525	//
526	// In its own file because `RecordingLanding+Microphone.swift` stood at 381
527	// lines against the 400-line cap for a new file; `view` and `trimmed` are
528	// the base file's, internal for it.
529	
530	import AppKit
531	
532	extension RecordingLanding {
533	    /// One stretch of the picture track: a landed segment's media, placed
534	    /// by `placeBackToBack`, or a gap of `Ticks` it leaves empty.
535	    enum PictureStretch {
536	        case picture(UInt32)
537	        case gap(Ticks)
538	    }
539	
540	    /// One stretch's microphone: its file when one landed (nil when none),
541	    /// and the offset its clip is placed by — a segment's measured
542	    /// `micOffset`, or 0 for a left-out voice.
543	    struct Voice {
544	        let descriptor: MediaDescriptor?
545	        let offset: Ticks
546	    }
547	
548	    /// One `Voice` per stretch of `result`, in order.
549	    static func voices(of result: RecordingResult) -> [Voice] {
550	        result.stretches.map { stretch in
551	            switch stretch {
552	            case .segment(let k):
553	                return Voice(
554	                    descriptor: result.segments[k].micDescriptor,
555	                    offset: result.segments[k].micOffset)
556	            case .voiceOnly(let i):
557	                return Voice(descriptor: result.unreadable[i].micDescriptor, offset: 0)
558	            }
559	        }
560	    }
561	
562	    /// One `PictureStretch` per stretch of `result`: segment `k`'s picture
563	    /// as `mediaIds[k]` (the ids its `add_media` answered, one per segment),
564	    /// and a left-out voice as a gap of `slotLength`, measured against the

---
title: Retime Range
description: Play the stretch between In and Out faster or slower on every unlocked track at once, and keep everything after it in step.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Retime Range plays the stretch between In and Out faster or slower on every unlocked track at once, and moves everything after Out up or back to stay in step. Use it to speed up a slow part of a screen recording with its microphone and camera together.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Retime Range…"
  tools="retime_range"
  needs="An in/out range."
/>

## Retime a range

<Steps>

1. Set [In and Out](/timeline/in-out-range/) around the stretch. The menu item is dimmed without them, and while another sheet is open.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Retime Range…**. It has no keyboard shortcut.

3. Set the **Rate**, and tick or untick **Preserve pitch**.

4. Choose **Apply**.

</Steps>

The whole edit is one undo step, **Retime Range**.

## The sheet

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Rate:** | How much faster the range plays. ×2 makes it half as long, and ×0.5 twice as long. The **Presets** pull-down offers 0.25×, 0.50×, 1×, 1.5×, 2×, 4×, 10× and 100×. | ×2 | ×0.1 to ×1000 |
| **Preserve pitch** | Sets the pitch setting on every video or audio clip in the range, as [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) does on one clip. | As the first video or audio clip on an unlocked track in the range has it, or on when there is none | |

**Apply** at ×1 closes the sheet and changes nothing. At any other rate it retimes the range.

If the rate takes a clip with sound past ×12, Frame Job [asks first](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/), because above ×12 a clip's audio is left out. **Set Speed** closes the sheet and applies the edit. **Cancel** leaves the sheet open with nothing changed.

## What happens in the range

### Clips across an edge

A clip that crosses In or Out is cut there first, as [Split](/editing/splitting/) cuts it. Only the piece inside the range changes speed.

### Rates multiply

Each video or audio clip inside plays at its own rate times the **Rate**, so a ×2 clip retimed by ×2 plays at ×4. A [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/#scale-a-whole-ramp) keeps its shape, and every rate in it scales.

### Titles, shapes and stills

Titles, shapes, stills, images, graphics and adjustment clips inside are stretched or squeezed by the same amount. A graphic with a length of its own keeps it.

### Actions

Actions keep their place in each clip, at the same fraction of its length. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).

### Markers and detached sound

Markers inside the range move with the picture, and markers after it move with everything else. A detached sound linked to a moved clip moves with it.

## Inside a nest

Retime Range works inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), where it retimes the nest's own tracks and uses the nest's own In and Out. A nest has no markers of its own, so none moves.

## When a range can't be retimed

Nothing changes, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. Frame Job checks these in order and stops at the first one it meets:

| What stops it | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The rate is outside ×0.1 to ×1000. | The sheet's field keeps you inside this range, so this one comes up with an agent. |
| The range is under two frames. | Widen the range. |
| A locked track has a clip that ends after In. It would fall out of step. | [Unlock the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/), or move In past that clip. |
| The range touches a nest clip. | Move the range off it, or retime inside the nest. |
| The range touches a caption page with timed words. | Move the range off it. |
| The range touches half of a detached pair. | Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
| A transition touches the range. | Move the range off it, or remove the transition. |
| Two markers would land on the same time. | Move one of them first. |
| A clip would play faster than ×1000 or slower than ×0.1. The message names the clip and the rate. | Pick a gentler rate, or set the clip's own speed first. |
| A clip would be squeezed under one frame. The message names it. | Pick a gentler rate. |

A clip only has to overlap the range to count, so a nest or a detached clip that crosses In or Out stops the edit too.

## With an agent

`retime_range` makes the same edit, but it takes the range as times, so it needs no In and Out. It never asks about ×12: the clip's audio is left out, and the answer says so. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).

## Related

- [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/)
- [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/)
- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
- [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/)
## Sound is left out above ×12

The limit is the same with [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) on or off. At exactly ×12 the sound still plays, and at anything faster it doesn't. The picture carries on to the top of the speed range, ×1000.

The limit is fixed, and no setting changes it. It sits a margin below the speeds at which an export with sound can stall.

Nothing is deleted. Bring the clip back to ×12 or below and its sound returns.

## The alert

Before an edit takes a clip with sound from ×12 or below to above ×12, an alert asks first. For one clip it reads:

> “Interview” will be silent at ×16.
>
> Frame Job leaves a clip’s audio out above ×12. The picture still plays.

For several clips it counts them. It reads “3 clips will be silent at ×16.”, or “3 clips will be silent at their new speeds.” when their rates differ, and then “Frame Job leaves a clip’s audio out above ×12. The pictures still play.”

The alert is a question, not a block. You can always go ahead.

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Set Speed** | Makes the edit exactly as you asked. It's the default button, and it keeps this name when the edit is a ramp or a stretch. |
| **Cancel** | Changes nothing and adds no undo step. |

You're asked once. A clip that's already above ×12 isn't asked about again, even if you make it faster still. A clip whose sound is switched off, or whose file has no sound, isn't asked about at all.

## Where the alert appears

| You're using | If you choose **Cancel** |
| --- | --- |
| **Clip ▸ Speed…** | The sheet stays open. |
| **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** | The sheet stays open. |
| **Clip ▸ Retime Range…** | The sheet stays open. |
| **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** | The sheet stays open. |
| The [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/): **Rate**, its quick picks, **Keep pitch**, **Reset** or **Fit to** | The fields go back to what they showed. |
| The [⌥ rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) | The clip stays as it was before the drag. |

A stretch is put back when you let go, so nothing has changed while the question is up. **Set Speed** then applies it again.

Moving, resizing or removing an action can't raise the rate a clip names, so those edits never ask.

## Ramps and the ×12 rule

On a [ramped clip](/speed/speed-ramps/), Frame Job looks at the fastest rate the clip names anywhere. If any rate in the ramp is above ×12, the whole clip is silent, not only the fast part.
## Where the speech comes from

Frame Job detects speech in every file with sound when it's imported, on your Mac, with the same detection [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) uses.

Choosing **Speech** saves where that file's speech is in the project, in the same undo step. The preview, every export and an agent then all follow the same stretches. A file keeps the speech it was given and isn't detected again, so another clip of the same file uses the same stretches.

**Duck by** is greyed out, so you can't choose **Speech**, in two cases:

- A selected file's speech is still being detected. Try again in a moment.
- A selected clip isn't a clip of a file with sound, such as a nest or a title.

Relinking the clip's file to a shorter one keeps the speech that still fits. Relinking it to a file with no sound forgets the speech, and the clip no longer ducks anything.

A file with no speech in it ducks nothing.
