---
title: "Speed Up Typing"
description: "Play the typing in a screen recording faster, while speech and shortcuts stay at normal speed, as one undo step."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Speed Up Typing plays the typing in a screen recording faster, so a viewer doesn't sit through every keystroke. Frame Job finds the typing from the recording's cursor file, leaves anything spoken or any shortcut at normal speed, and makes the whole change one undo step.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…"
  where="New Recording panel ▸ When it lands ▸ Speed up typing"
  tools={['speed_up_typing', 'get_cursor_events']}
  needs="A screen recording made with Record shortcuts on. Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Speed up the typing

<Steps>

1. Select the clip. Select both halves if you've split the recording, and any other recordings you want done at the same time.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…**. It has no keyboard shortcut. The sheet reads "Reading cursor files…" for a moment, with **Apply** dimmed.

3. Set [**Rate**, **Shortest stretch** and **Keep pitch**](#the-settings).

4. Read the summary under the settings, for example "2 typing stretches sped up ×4, saving 9.3 s."

5. Choose **Apply**, or **Cancel** to leave the timeline as it was.

</Steps>

The menu item is dimmed unless every selected clip is a movie with a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). It's also dimmed while another sheet is open. It works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), on the nest's own clips and tracks.

The edit is one undo step, **Speed Up Typing**.

To do this for every recording as it arrives, tick **Speed up typing** in the recorder panel. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/#speed-up-typing).

## What counts as typing

A typing stretch is a run of at least 3 typed keys, each less than 1 s after the last. It lasts from the first key to the last.

The keys come from the recording's cursor file, which only holds them if the recording was made with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on. Without it the menu item still works, but the sheet finds no typing. The file holds when you typed, never what you typed, and nothing is noted while an app holds secure input, such as a password field.

Only typing in the part of the clip you've kept counts. Typing you've trimmed away is ignored.

## The settings

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Rate:** | How much faster the typing plays. | ×4 | ×2 to ×8 |
| **Shortest stretch:** | Typing shorter than this is left alone. | 3 s | 1 to 30 s |
| **Keep pitch** | Keeps the sped-up sound at its own pitch. Off, it rises like a fast tape. See [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/). | On | |

The two number fields take up to two decimal places, and their values stay inside the range. The summary updates when you leave a field or change **Keep pitch**.

Frame Job remembers these from one use to the next. It saves a setting when you apply the edit, and only if you changed it, so **Cancel** saves nothing.

## What the sheet tells you

The sheet says what **Apply** would do before you press it, or why nothing would happen.

| The sheet says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "2 typing stretches sped up ×4, saving 9.3 s." | What **Apply** will do. |
| "No typing stretch without speech or a shortcut lasts 3 s or more in the selected clips, so nothing would change." | There's nothing to speed. **Apply** stays dimmed. Try a lower **Shortest stretch**. The figure in the sentence follows that setting. |
| "Waiting for speech detection on …" | Frame Job is still finding the speech in the files it names. **Apply** is dimmed, and the sheet updates by itself. |
| "Speech detection has not finished for … Close this sheet and try again." | It waited 5 minutes and stopped. |
| "… is offline, so its speech cannot be read." | A file under a stretch is missing, so nothing changes. [Relink it](/projects/import-media/) first. |
| "Speech detection is unavailable on this Mac, so Speed Up Typing cannot tell typing from talking." | Speech detection can't run here, so nothing changes. |
| "The typing from … cannot be sped up: …" | One stretch can't be sped. See [When it can't speed up](#when-it-cant-speed-up). |

## What stays at normal speed

From each stretch, Frame Job takes out every moment of speech and every shortcut. What's left is sped up, if it still lasts as long as **Shortest stretch**.

### Speech

Any part of a stretch with speech under it stays at normal speed. That goes for every clip of a file with sound under the stretch, on any track, even if the clip is muted. So a voice on the Microphone track holds the typing back just as sound in the movie does.

The speech comes from the same on-device detection [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/#where-the-speech-comes-from) uses. If a file has no saved speech, Frame Job saves it with the project in the same undo step. If detection hasn't finished, the sheet starts it and waits.

### Shortcuts

A recorded shortcut and its overlay are never sped up, so that a viewer can read the overlay. Frame Job takes out the overlay's whole clip on a track named **Shortcuts**, or 1.5 s from the press when there's no overlay.

[Add the overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) first. Otherwise a longer overlay added afterwards sits over typing that's already been sped up.

### The edges

Each sped stretch keeps 0.3 s at normal speed at both ends, so the change in pace isn't abrupt. **Shortest stretch** is measured before those edges come off. A 3 s stretch at ×4 speeds its middle 2.4 s down to 0.6 s, which saves 1.8 s. Cuts then land on frames, so the figures can differ slightly.

## What the edit does to the timeline

Each stretch is sped with [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) on every unlocked track, so the camera and the microphone stay in sync with the screen and everything after moves up. A title or a graphic over a stretch is squeezed by the same amount, as Retime Range does it.

The sound in a sped stretch is sped too, because it's cut and retimed with the picture.

### Split recordings

The halves of a recording you split are treated as one when you select them both and they touch, so typing across the cut is one stretch. With one half selected, Frame Job only looks at that half.

## If a clip would go silent

Rates multiply, so a clip already playing at ×2 goes to ×16 at a **Rate** of ×8. Frame Job leaves a clip's sound out above ×12, so when **Apply** would take a clip with sound past that, an alert asks first.

**Set Speed** goes ahead. **Cancel** leaves the sheet open with nothing changed, so you can lower the **Rate**. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).

## When it can't speed up

Speed Up Typing is all or nothing. If any stretch can't be sped, nothing changes, **Apply** is dimmed, and the sheet names the stretch and the reason in place of the summary.

| What stops it | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| A locked track has a clip that ends after the stretch begins. | [Unlock the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
| A transition touches the stretch. | Remove the [transition](/motion/add-a-transition/). |
| Half of a detached pair is in the stretch. | Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
| A selected clip plays reversed. The sheet reads "Clip … plays reversed; Speed Up Typing speeds only clips that play forward." | Leave that clip out, or [turn off Reverse](/speed/reverse/). |
| The cursor file is missing or won't read. | Point the clip at its file again. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/). |

A stretch can also be stopped by anything else that stops Retime Range, such as a nest clip or a caption page with timed words. See [When a range can't be retimed](/speed/retime-range/#when-a-range-cant-be-retimed).

- It can limit the edit to part of the timeline, which the sheet can't.
- It doesn't remember anything. It starts from ×4, 3 s and pitch kept unless told otherwise.
- It doesn't wait for speech detection. It says the speech hasn't been detected yet, and to try again in a moment.
- It never asks about ×12. The clip's sound is left out and the answer says so.

---
title: "Speed Up Typing"
description: "Play the typing in a screen recording faster, while speech and shortcuts stay at normal speed, as one undo step."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Speed Up Typing plays the typing in a screen recording faster, so a viewer doesn't sit through every keystroke. Frame Job finds the typing from the recording's cursor file, leaves anything spoken or any shortcut at normal speed, and makes the whole change one undo step.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…"
  where="New Recording panel ▸ When it lands ▸ Speed up typing"
  tools={['speed_up_typing', 'get_cursor_events']}
  needs="A screen recording made with Record shortcuts on. Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Speed up the typing

<Steps>

1. Select the clip. Select both halves if you've split the recording, and any other recordings you want done at the same time.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…**. It has no keyboard shortcut. The sheet reads "Reading cursor files…" for a moment, with **Apply** dimmed.

3. Set [**Rate**, **Shortest stretch** and **Keep pitch**](#the-settings).

4. Read the summary under the settings, for example "2 typing stretches sped up ×4, saving 9.3 s."

5. Choose **Apply**, or **Cancel** to leave the timeline as it was.

</Steps>

The menu item is dimmed unless every selected clip is a movie with a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). It's also dimmed while another sheet is open. It works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), on the nest's own clips and tracks.

The edit is one undo step, **Speed Up Typing**.

To do this for every recording as it arrives, tick **Speed up typing** in the recorder panel. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/#speed-up-typing).

## What counts as typing

A typing stretch is a run of at least 3 typed keys, each less than 1 s after the last. It lasts from the first key to the last.

The keys come from the recording's cursor file, which only holds them if the recording was made with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on. Without it the menu item still works, but the sheet finds no typing. The file holds when you typed, never what you typed, and nothing is noted while an app holds secure input, such as a password field.

Only typing in the part of the clip you've kept counts. Typing you've trimmed away is ignored.

## The settings

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Rate:** | How much faster the typing plays. | ×4 | ×2 to ×8 |
| **Shortest stretch:** | Typing shorter than this is left alone. | 3 s | 1 to 30 s |
| **Keep pitch** | Keeps the sped-up sound at its own pitch. Off, it rises like a fast tape. See [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/). | On | |

The two number fields take up to two decimal places, and their values stay inside the range. The summary updates when you leave a field or change **Keep pitch**.

Frame Job remembers these from one use to the next. It saves a setting when you apply the edit, and only if you changed it, so **Cancel** saves nothing.

## What the sheet tells you

The sheet says what **Apply** would do before you press it, or why nothing would happen.

| The sheet says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "2 typing stretches sped up ×4, saving 9.3 s." | What **Apply** will do. |
| "No typing stretch without speech or a shortcut lasts 3 s or more in the selected clips, so nothing would change." | There's nothing to speed. **Apply** stays dimmed. Try a lower **Shortest stretch**. The figure in the sentence follows that setting. |
| "Waiting for speech detection on …" | Frame Job is still finding the speech in the files it names. **Apply** is dimmed, and the sheet updates by itself. |
| "Speech detection has not finished for … Close this sheet and try again." | It waited 5 minutes and stopped. |
| "… is offline, so its speech cannot be read." | A file under a stretch is missing, so nothing changes. [Relink it](/projects/import-media/) first. |
| "Speech detection is unavailable on this Mac, so Speed Up Typing cannot tell typing from talking." | Speech detection can't run here, so nothing changes. |
| "The typing from … cannot be sped up: …" | One stretch can't be sped. See [When it can't speed up](#when-it-cant-speed-up). |

## What stays at normal speed

From each stretch, Frame Job takes out every moment of speech and every shortcut. What's left is sped up, if it still lasts as long as **Shortest stretch**.

### Speech

Any part of a stretch with speech under it stays at normal speed. That goes for every clip of a file with sound under the stretch, on any track, even if the clip is muted. So a voice on the Microphone track holds the typing back just as sound in the movie does.

The speech comes from the same on-device detection [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/#where-the-speech-comes-from) uses. If a file has no saved speech, Frame Job saves it with the project in the same undo step. If detection hasn't finished, the sheet starts it and waits.

### Shortcuts

A recorded shortcut and its overlay are never sped up, so that a viewer can read the overlay. Frame Job takes out the overlay's whole clip on a track named **Shortcuts**, or 1.5 s from the press when there's no overlay.

[Add the overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) first. Otherwise a longer overlay added afterwards sits over typing that's already been sped up.

### The edges

Each sped stretch keeps 0.3 s at normal speed at both ends, so the change in pace isn't abrupt. **Shortest stretch** is measured before those edges come off. A 3 s stretch at ×4 speeds its middle 2.4 s down to 0.6 s, which saves 1.8 s. Cuts then land on frames, so the figures can differ slightly.

## What the edit does to the timeline

Each stretch is sped with [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) on every unlocked track, so the camera and the microphone stay in sync with the screen and everything after moves up. A title or a graphic over a stretch is squeezed by the same amount, as Retime Range does it.

The sound in a sped stretch is sped too, because it's cut and retimed with the picture.

### Split recordings

The halves of a recording you split are treated as one when you select them both and they touch, so typing across the cut is one stretch. With one half selected, Frame Job only looks at that half.

## If a clip would go silent

Rates multiply, so a clip already playing at ×2 goes to ×16 at a **Rate** of ×8. Frame Job leaves a clip's sound out above ×12, so when **Apply** would take a clip with sound past that, an alert asks first.

**Set Speed** goes ahead. **Cancel** leaves the sheet open with nothing changed, so you can lower the **Rate**. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).

## When it can't speed up

Speed Up Typing is all or nothing. If any stretch can't be sped, nothing changes, **Apply** is dimmed, and the sheet names the stretch and the reason in place of the summary.

| What stops it | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| A locked track has a clip that ends after the stretch begins. | [Unlock the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
| A transition touches the stretch. | Remove the [transition](/motion/add-a-transition/). |
| Half of a detached pair is in the stretch. | Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
| A selected clip plays reversed. The sheet reads "Clip … plays reversed; Speed Up Typing speeds only clips that play forward." | Leave that clip out, or [turn off Reverse](/speed/reverse/). |
| The cursor file is missing or won't read. | Point the clip at its file again. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/). |

A stretch can also be stopped by anything else that stops Retime Range, such as a nest clip or a caption page with timed words. See [When a range can't be retimed](/speed/retime-range/#when-a-range-cant-be-retimed).

## With an agent

`speed_up_typing` makes the same edit, with these differences:

- It can limit the edit to part of the timeline, which the sheet can't.
- It doesn't remember anything. It starts from ×4, 3 s and pitch kept unless told otherwise.
- It doesn't wait for speech detection. It says the speech hasn't been detected yet, and to try again in a moment.
- It never asks about ×12. The clip's sound is left out and the answer says so.

`get_cursor_events` reads a recording's typing stretches and changes nothing. See [Tools: recording and screencasts](/mcp/tools-recording/).

## Related

- [Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/)
- [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/)
- [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/)

---
title: "Recording permissions"
description: "Which macOS permissions a recording needs, when Frame Job asks for each one, and what to do when one is missing."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A recording can need up to four macOS permissions, depending on what you record. Frame Job asks for them only when you press **Record** in the recorder panel, and never during a countdown.

<AtAGlance
  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Record', 'System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security']}
  tools="record_screen"
  needs="macOS's Screen Recording, Input Monitoring, Camera and Microphone permissions, as the table below says."
/>

## Which permissions you need

| Permission | Needed when | Where it lives in **System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security** | Relaunch afterwards? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Screen Recording** | You record a display or a window. | **Screen & System Audio Recording** | If macOS asks |
| **Input Monitoring** | **Record shortcuts** is ticked and you record a display or a window. | **Input Monitoring** | No |
| **Camera** | **Source** is **Camera**, or **Record the camera too** is ticked. | **Camera** | Yes, after a denial |
| **Microphone** | A microphone is chosen, which every voice-over needs. | **Microphone** | Yes, after a denial |

A camera on its own or a voice-over doesn't need Screen Recording. Frame Job never needs Accessibility.

## When Frame Job asks

A press of **Record** reads every permission it needs before the countdown begins, so a countdown never ends in a prompt. If one is missing, that press stops there, and the panel's note says what to do. The recorder panel is the only place Frame Job asks for these or opens System Settings for them.

The checks run in a fixed order, and stop at the first one missing:

| You're recording | The order |
| --- | --- |
| A display or a window | Screen Recording, Input Monitoring, Camera, Microphone |
| A camera on its own | Camera, Microphone |
| A voice-over | Microphone |

Frame Job skips any that the recording doesn't need. Before any of them, it checks that you've picked what to record: a window, a camera, or a microphone for a voice-over.

## Screen Recording

The first press of **Record** without the permission shows macOS's prompt. The panel's note reads:

> Screen Recording is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording, then relaunch.

Turn it on, relaunch Frame Job if macOS asks you to, and press **Record** again.

macOS shows that prompt only once, and Frame Job remembers it has asked. Every later press without the permission opens System Settings at the right pane instead, and the note adds "System Settings is open at that pane."

## Input Monitoring

**Record shortcuts** needs Input Monitoring to see key presses. macOS shows no prompt for it, and Frame Job isn't in that pane's list until you add it. So a press of **Record** without it opens System Settings at the pane, and the note reads:

> Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring. If Frame Job is not in its list, add it with +.

Turn Frame Job on there, adding it with **+** if it isn't listed, and press **Record** again. No relaunch is needed.

## Camera

If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears. It reads "Frame Job records the camera you choose, into a file of its own. Nothing is sent anywhere."

- **Allow** carries on to the microphone check and the countdown.
- **Don't Allow** leaves the panel idle, with a note saying the camera isn't granted.

If you've denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Camera pane instead, and the note says so. Turn it on there and relaunch Frame Job.

## Microphone

If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears. It reads "Frame Job records the microphone you choose alongside a screen recording, into a file of its own beside the movie. Nothing is sent anywhere."

- **Allow** starts the countdown straight away, as long as the panel is still open.
- **Don't Allow** leaves the panel idle, with a note saying the microphone isn't granted.

If you've denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Microphone pane instead, and the note says so. Turn it on there and relaunch Frame Job.

## If you started Frame Job from a terminal

A Frame Job started from a terminal or another app runs under that app's permissions, not its own. Turning on Frame Job in System Settings then makes no difference.

The panel's note says so, and names the process that launched it by its pid:

> This Frame Job was launched by another process (pid 4182), so the grant that counts is that application's — the terminal's, for a shell launch; or relaunch with open -a "Frame Job".

Either give the permission to that app, or quit Frame Job and start it from the Finder, the Dock or `open -a "Frame Job"`.

In a launch like this, Frame Job doesn't remember having asked. Each press without Screen Recording shows the prompt again rather than opening System Settings.

## The panel steps aside

The recorder panel usually floats above other windows. While a macOS prompt or System Settings is up, it stops floating so that it doesn't cover them. It floats again on your next press of **Record**, or when you open the panel again.

## macOS's recurring alert

macOS periodically asks whether to keep letting Frame Job record the screen. Frame Job can't see this alert, and the permission still reads as granted, so a capture waiting behind it looks like a recording that won't start.

If the panel stays on **Starting…** and then says "The recording did not start within 20 s.", look for the alert on the screen. Answer it and press **Record** again.

## With an agent

`record_screen` never asks for a permission and never opens System Settings, because a prompt needs a person in front of it. It reads each permission it needs and, if one is missing, stops with the same sentence, naming the pane. Grant it once from the panel.

If the recording doesn't start or finish in time, its answer says a macOS alert may be waiting. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)
- [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/)
- [Record a camera](/recording/record-a-camera/)
- [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/)
- [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/)

---
title: "When a recording stops on its own"
description: "What Frame Job keeps when a camera, a microphone or the system stops a recording, and what to do when a recording can't be added."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A recording can lose a device or end without you pressing Stop. Frame Job keeps what it captured, and tells you what happened. This page says what lands in each case, and what to do about what doesn't.

<AtAGlance
  where={["The recorder panel's note", 'The menu-bar item']}
  tools="record_screen"
/>

## Where you'll read about it

Everything here is reported in the note on the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/). A recording that lands cleanly doesn't bring the panel back, but one with something to say does, as long as the panel was on screen when the recording began.

If the panel wasn't on screen, press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> to open it and read the note.

While a display or a window records, the panel is hidden, so the note only appears when the recording lands. While a camera on its own or a voice-over records, the panel stays up, so the note appears as it happens.

## What's kept

| What happened | Does the recording go on? | What lands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [A camera on its own stops](#a-camera-stops) | No | What was captured |
| [A camera beside the screen stops](#a-camera-stops) | Yes | The screen, and the camera up to the stop |
| [The microphone stops](#a-microphone-stops) | Yes | The picture, without that microphone file |
| [A voice-over's microphone stops](#a-voice-overs-microphone-stops) | No | What was recorded |
| [The display sleeps or goes away](#the-display-sleeps-or-the-system-stops-the-recording) | No | What was captured |
| [A stretch's movie won't read](#a-stretch-wont-read) | It has already ended | Every other stretch, and that stretch's voice if it reads |
| [A file is too short for a frame](#a-file-is-too-short-for-one-frame) | It has already ended | That file in the media list, and the rest as usual |
| [The recording can't be added](#the-recording-cant-be-added) | It has already ended | Nothing, but the files stay on disk |

## A camera stops

If a camera recording's camera stops, for example because it's unplugged, the recording ends there and what was captured lands. The note gives the reason, then "What was captured was added.":

> The camera FaceTime HD Camera stopped on its own: it was disconnected. What was captured was added.

It can also read "its session was interrupted", or give a reason from macOS.

Beside the screen, a camera that stops doesn't end the recording. The screen keeps recording, what the camera wrote up to then lands, and the note gives the same reason. Later stretches after a pause have no camera. The one exception is a camera that fails while the recording is still starting, which stops the start with that sentence.

If a camera hasn't settled at its rate when the recording begins, the recording begins anyway and the note says what it ran at:

> The camera ran at 24.0 fps, not its 30, in the 1 s it was given to settle; the recording began anyway.

## A microphone stops

A microphone that stops partway through a screen or camera recording doesn't end it. The picture keeps recording and the panel's level meter goes silent. With the panel on screen, its note says so at once:

> The microphone stopped: … The picture is still recording.

The picture lands either way. If the microphone's file didn't finish properly or won't read, it isn't added, and the note says why and where the file is, so you can [import it](/projects/import-media/) yourself. The same goes for a microphone that never started, which reads "The microphone never started recording, so the picture was recorded without it."

## A voice-over's microphone stops

A voice-over has nothing else to record, so if its microphone stops on its own, for example because it's unplugged, the voice-over ends there. What was recorded lands, with a note:

> The microphone stopped recording on its own: … The voice-over ends where it stopped.

## The display sleeps or the system stops the recording

If the display sleeps or goes away, or the system stops the recording, what was captured lands, with the note:

> The system stopped the recording (the display slept or went away); what was captured was added.

Stopping from macOS's own screen-recording indicator in the menu bar also lands the recording. The note reads "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added."

## The screen is locked

If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, no display can be shared, so a display recording can't start until one wakes. The panel's note says the display isn't shareable.

## Resume doesn't work

If **Resume Recording** fails, the recording stays paused and nothing is lost. No file is taking the picture until a resume works, so you can try again, or stop and land what you have.

The reason goes in the panel's note. During a voice-over or a camera recording it appears there at once. During a screen recording it appears when the recording lands, and the panel comes back to show it.

A **Pause Recording** that fails only beeps, because the recording is still running.

## A stretch won't read

Each stretch between pauses has its own movie. If one won't read, for example an empty file from a pause right after a resume, it's left out, and the stretches that do read land. The note names the file and everything it left on disk:

> A segment was left out. … Its files are kept at …

Only a recording with no readable movie at all fails, and its note names every file.

### Its voice still lands

If a left-out stretch's microphone file reads, it lands without its picture, on the Microphone track in the slot the picture would have had. The picture track keeps a gap there, and the next picture starts after it. The note reads "The left-out segment's microphone, …, was added to the project without its picture."

That stretch's camera file stays on disk and the note names it, but it isn't added.

In a new project, a left-out voice from before the first picture has no timeline to sit on, so it lands in the media list without a clip, and the note says so.

## A file is too short for one frame

A file too short for one frame can't become a clip. It lands in the media list, the rest of the recording lands as usual, and the note says so:

> … is too short for a frame (12 ms) and was added to the media list without a clip.

## The recording can't be added

If a recording can't be added, nothing goes on the timeline, but the files are safe. The note names every one, so you can [import them](/projects/import-media/):

> The recording was saved at … but could not be added: …

These are the usual reasons:

| What happened | What to do |
| --- | --- |

---
title: "When a recording stops on its own"
description: "What Frame Job keeps when a camera, a microphone or the system stops a recording, and what to do when a recording can't be added."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A recording can lose a device or end without you pressing Stop. Frame Job keeps what it captured, and tells you what happened. This page says what lands in each case, and what to do about what doesn't.

<AtAGlance
  where={["The recorder panel's note", 'The menu-bar item']}
  tools="record_screen"
/>

## Where you'll read about it

Everything here is reported in the note on the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/). A recording that lands cleanly doesn't bring the panel back, but one with something to say does, as long as the panel was on screen when the recording began.

If the panel wasn't on screen, press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> to open it and read the note.

While a display or a window records, the panel is hidden, so the note only appears when the recording lands. While a camera on its own or a voice-over records, the panel stays up, so the note appears as it happens.

## What's kept

| What happened | Does the recording go on? | What lands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [A camera on its own stops](#a-camera-stops) | No | What was captured |
| [A camera beside the screen stops](#a-camera-stops) | Yes | The screen, and the camera up to the stop |
| [The microphone stops](#a-microphone-stops) | Yes | The picture, without that microphone file |
| [A voice-over's microphone stops](#a-voice-overs-microphone-stops) | No | What was recorded |
| [The display sleeps or goes away](#the-display-sleeps-or-the-system-stops-the-recording) | No | What was captured |
| [A stretch's movie won't read](#a-stretch-wont-read) | It has already ended | Every other stretch, and that stretch's voice if it reads |
| [A file is too short for a frame](#a-file-is-too-short-for-one-frame) | It has already ended | That file in the media list, and the rest as usual |
| [The recording can't be added](#the-recording-cant-be-added) | It has already ended | Nothing, but the files stay on disk |

## A camera stops

If a camera recording's camera stops, for example because it's unplugged, the recording ends there and what was captured lands. The note gives the reason, then "What was captured was added.":

> The camera FaceTime HD Camera stopped on its own: it was disconnected. What was captured was added.

It can also read "its session was interrupted", or give a reason from macOS.

Beside the screen, a camera that stops doesn't end the recording. The screen keeps recording, what the camera wrote up to then lands, and the note gives the same reason. Later stretches after a pause have no camera. The one exception is a camera that fails while the recording is still starting, which stops the start with that sentence.

If a camera hasn't settled at its rate when the recording begins, the recording begins anyway and the note says what it ran at:

> The camera ran at 24.0 fps, not its 30, in the 1 s it was given to settle; the recording began anyway.

## A microphone stops

A microphone that stops partway through a screen or camera recording doesn't end it. The picture keeps recording and the panel's level meter goes silent. With the panel on screen, its note says so at once:

> The microphone stopped: … The picture is still recording.

The picture lands either way. If the microphone's file didn't finish properly or won't read, it isn't added, and the note says why and where the file is, so you can [import it](/projects/import-media/) yourself. The same goes for a microphone that never started, which reads "The microphone never started recording, so the picture was recorded without it."

## A voice-over's microphone stops

A voice-over has nothing else to record, so if its microphone stops on its own, for example because it's unplugged, the voice-over ends there. What was recorded lands, with a note:

> The microphone stopped recording on its own: … The voice-over ends where it stopped.

## The display sleeps or the system stops the recording

If the display sleeps or goes away, or the system stops the recording, what was captured lands, with the note:

> The system stopped the recording (the display slept or went away); what was captured was added.

Stopping from macOS's own screen-recording indicator in the menu bar also lands the recording. The note reads "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added."

## The screen is locked

If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, no display can be shared, so a display recording can't start until one wakes. The panel's note says the display isn't shareable.

## Resume doesn't work

If **Resume Recording** fails, the recording stays paused and nothing is lost. No file is taking the picture until a resume works, so you can try again, or stop and land what you have.

The reason goes in the panel's note. During a voice-over or a camera recording it appears there at once. During a screen recording it appears when the recording lands, and the panel comes back to show it.

A **Pause Recording** that fails only beeps, because the recording is still running.

## A stretch won't read

Each stretch between pauses has its own movie. If one won't read, for example an empty file from a pause right after a resume, it's left out, and the stretches that do read land. The note names the file and everything it left on disk:

> A segment was left out. … Its files are kept at …

Only a recording with no readable movie at all fails, and its note names every file.

### Its voice still lands

If a left-out stretch's microphone file reads, it lands without its picture, on the Microphone track in the slot the picture would have had. The picture track keeps a gap there, and the next picture starts after it. The note reads "The left-out segment's microphone, …, was added to the project without its picture."

That stretch's camera file stays on disk and the note names it, but it isn't added.

In a new project, a left-out voice from before the first picture has no timeline to sit on, so it lands in the media list without a clip, and the note says so.

## A file is too short for one frame

A file too short for one frame can't become a clip. It lands in the media list, the rest of the recording lands as usual, and the note says so:

> … is too short for a frame (12 ms) and was added to the media list without a clip.

## The recording can't be added

If a recording can't be added, nothing goes on the timeline, but the files are safe. The note names every one, so you can [import them](/projects/import-media/):

> The recording was saved at … but could not be added: …

These are the usual reasons:

| What happened | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The project is at its limit of 64 tracks and the recording needs a new one. If the picture would fit but the microphone wouldn't, none of it is added. | [Delete a track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) you don't need, then import the files. |
| You were still dragging on the timeline. Frame Job waits for a drag to end, for up to 20 s. | Import the files. |

If the files don't finish writing within 10 s of Stop, the note reads "The recording did not finish writing within 10 s." and names the files kept on disk.

## Very long recordings

A recording longer than 9:59:59 carries on as usual, but the menu-bar item's label gets wider than the item was sized for.

## With an agent

`record_screen` reports all of this in its answer, so an agent can tell what stopped and what landed. With the screen locked, it stops before recording and says that no display is shareable. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

- [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/)
- [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/)
- [The menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

---
title: "Speed Up Typing"
description: "Play the typing in a screen recording faster, while speech and shortcuts stay at normal speed, as one undo step."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Speed Up Typing plays the typing in a screen recording faster, so a viewer doesn't sit through every keystroke. Frame Job finds the typing from the recording's cursor file, leaves anything spoken or any shortcut at normal speed, and makes the whole change one undo step.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…"
  where="New Recording panel ▸ When it lands ▸ Speed up typing"
  tools={['speed_up_typing', 'get_cursor_events']}
  needs="A screen recording made with Record shortcuts on. Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Speed up the typing

<Steps>

1. Select the clip. Select both halves if you've split the recording, and any other recordings you want done at the same time.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…**. It has no keyboard shortcut. The sheet reads "Reading cursor files…" for a moment, with **Apply** dimmed.

3. Set [**Rate**, **Shortest stretch** and **Keep pitch**](#the-settings).

4. Read the summary under the settings, for example "2 typing stretches sped up ×4, saving 9.3 s."

5. Choose **Apply**, or **Cancel** to leave the timeline as it was.

</Steps>

The menu item is dimmed unless every selected clip is a movie with a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). It's also dimmed while another sheet is open. It works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), on the nest's own clips and tracks.

The edit is one undo step, **Speed Up Typing**.

To do this for every recording as it arrives, tick **Speed up typing** in the recorder panel. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/#speed-up-typing).

## What counts as typing

A typing stretch is a run of at least 3 typed keys, each less than 1 s after the last. It lasts from the first key to the last.

The keys come from the recording's cursor file, which only holds them if the recording was made with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on. Without it the menu item still works, but the sheet finds no typing. The file holds when you typed, never what you typed, and nothing is noted while an app holds secure input, such as a password field.

Only typing in the part of the clip you've kept counts. Typing you've trimmed away is ignored.

## The settings

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Rate:** | How much faster the typing plays. | ×4 | ×2 to ×8 |
| **Shortest stretch:** | Typing shorter than this is left alone. | 3 s | 1 to 30 s |
| **Keep pitch** | Keeps the sped-up sound at its own pitch. Off, it rises like a fast tape. See [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/). | On | |

The two number fields take up to two decimal places, and their values stay inside the range. The summary updates when you leave a field or change **Keep pitch**.

Frame Job remembers these from one use to the next. It saves a setting when you apply the edit, and only if you changed it, so **Cancel** saves nothing.

## What the sheet tells you

The sheet says what **Apply** would do before you press it, or why nothing would happen.

| The sheet says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "2 typing stretches sped up ×4, saving 9.3 s." | What **Apply** will do. |
| "No typing stretch without speech or a shortcut lasts 3 s or more in the selected clips, so nothing would change." | There's nothing to speed. **Apply** stays dimmed. Try a lower **Shortest stretch**. The figure in the sentence follows that setting. |
| "Waiting for speech detection on …" | Frame Job is still finding the speech in the files it names. **Apply** is dimmed, and the sheet updates by itself. |
| "Speech detection has not finished for … Close this sheet and try again." | It waited 5 minutes and stopped. |
| "… is offline, so its speech cannot be read." | A file under a stretch is missing, so nothing changes. [Relink it](/projects/import-media/) first. |
| "Speech detection is unavailable on this Mac, so Speed Up Typing cannot tell typing from talking." | Speech detection can't run here, so nothing changes. |
| "The typing from … cannot be sped up: …" | One stretch can't be sped. See [When it can't speed up](#when-it-cant-speed-up). |

## What stays at normal speed

From each stretch, Frame Job takes out every moment of speech and every shortcut. What's left is sped up, if it still lasts as long as **Shortest stretch**.

### Speech

Any part of a stretch with speech under it stays at normal speed. That goes for every clip of a file with sound under the stretch, on any track, even if the clip is muted. So a voice on the Microphone track holds the typing back just as sound in the movie does.

The speech comes from the same on-device detection [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/#where-the-speech-comes-from) uses. If a file has no saved speech, Frame Job saves it with the project in the same undo step. If detection hasn't finished, the sheet starts it and waits.

### Shortcuts

A recorded shortcut and its overlay are never sped up, so that a viewer can read the overlay. Frame Job takes out the overlay's whole clip on a track named **Shortcuts**, or 1.5 s from the press when there's no overlay.

[Add the overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) first. Otherwise a longer overlay added afterwards sits over typing that's already been sped up.

### The edges

Each sped stretch keeps 0.3 s at normal speed at both ends, so the change in pace isn't abrupt. **Shortest stretch** is measured before those edges come off. A 3 s stretch at ×4 speeds its middle 2.4 s down to 0.6 s, which saves 1.8 s. Cuts then land on frames, so the figures can differ slightly.

## What the edit does to the timeline

Each stretch is sped with [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) on every unlocked track, so the camera and the microphone stay in sync with the screen and everything after moves up. A title or a graphic over a stretch is squeezed by the same amount, as Retime Range does it.

The sound in a sped stretch is sped too, because it's cut and retimed with the picture.

### Split recordings

The halves of a recording you split are treated as one when you select them both and they touch, so typing across the cut is one stretch. With one half selected, Frame Job only looks at that half.

## If a clip would go silent

Rates multiply, so a clip already playing at ×2 goes to ×16 at a **Rate** of ×8. Frame Job leaves a clip's sound out above ×12, so when **Apply** would take a clip with sound past that, an alert asks first.

**Set Speed** goes ahead. **Cancel** leaves the sheet open with nothing changed, so you can lower the **Rate**. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).

## When it can't speed up

Speed Up Typing is all or nothing. If any stretch can't be sped, nothing changes, **Apply** is dimmed, and the sheet names the stretch and the reason in place of the summary.

| What stops it | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| A locked track has a clip that ends after the stretch begins. | [Unlock the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
| A transition touches the stretch. | Remove the [transition](/motion/add-a-transition/). |
| Half of a detached pair is in the stretch. | Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
| A selected clip plays reversed. The sheet reads "Clip … plays reversed; Speed Up Typing speeds only clips that play forward." | Leave that clip out, or [turn off Reverse](/speed/reverse/). |
| The cursor file is missing or won't read. | Point the clip at its file again. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/). |

A stretch can also be stopped by anything else that stops Retime Range, such as a nest clip or a caption page with timed words. See [When a range can't be retimed](/speed/retime-range/#when-a-range-cant-be-retimed).

## With an agent

`speed_up_typing` makes the same edit, with these differences:

- It can limit the edit to part of the timeline, which the sheet can't.
- It doesn't remember anything. It starts from ×4, 3 s and pitch kept unless told otherwise.
- It doesn't wait for speech detection. It says the speech hasn't been detected yet, and to try again in a moment.
- It never asks about ×12. The clip's sound is left out and the answer says so.

`get_cursor_events` reads a recording's typing stretches and changes nothing. See [Tools: recording and screencasts](/mcp/tools-recording/).

## Related

- [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/)
- [Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/)
- [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/)
- [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/)
- [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/)

---
title: "Recording permissions"
description: "Which macOS permissions a recording needs, when Frame Job asks for each one, and what to do when one is missing."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A recording can need up to four macOS permissions, depending on what you record. Frame Job asks for them only when you press **Record** in the recorder panel, and never during a countdown.

<AtAGlance
  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Record', 'System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security']}
  tools="record_screen"
  needs="macOS's Screen Recording, Input Monitoring, Camera and Microphone permissions, as the table below says."
/>

## Which permissions you need

| Permission | Needed when | Where it lives in **System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security** | Relaunch afterwards? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Screen Recording** | You record a display or a window. | **Screen & System Audio Recording** | If macOS asks |
| **Input Monitoring** | **Record shortcuts** is ticked and you record a display or a window. | **Input Monitoring** | No |
| **Camera** | **Source** is **Camera**, or **Record the camera too** is ticked. | **Camera** | Yes, after a denial |
| **Microphone** | A microphone is chosen, which every voice-over needs. | **Microphone** | Yes, after a denial |

A camera on its own or a voice-over doesn't need Screen Recording. Frame Job never needs Accessibility.

## When Frame Job asks

A press of **Record** reads every permission it needs before the countdown begins, so a countdown never ends in a prompt. If one is missing, that press stops there, and the panel's note says what to do. The recorder panel is the only place Frame Job asks for these or opens System Settings for them.

The checks run in a fixed order, and stop at the first one missing:

| You're recording | The order |
| --- | --- |
| A display or a window | Screen Recording, Input Monitoring, Camera, Microphone |
| A camera on its own | Camera, Microphone |
| A voice-over | Microphone |

Frame Job skips any that the recording doesn't need. Before any of them, it checks that you've picked what to record: a window, a camera, or a microphone for a voice-over.

## Screen Recording

The first press of **Record** without the permission shows macOS's prompt. The panel's note reads:

> Screen Recording is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording, then relaunch.

Turn it on, relaunch Frame Job if macOS asks you to, and press **Record** again.

macOS shows that prompt only once, and Frame Job remembers it has asked. Every later press without the permission opens System Settings at the right pane instead, and the note adds "System Settings is open at that pane."

## Input Monitoring

**Record shortcuts** needs Input Monitoring to see key presses. macOS shows no prompt for it, and Frame Job isn't in that pane's list until you add it. So a press of **Record** without it opens System Settings at the pane, and the note reads:

> Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring. If Frame Job is not in its list, add it with +.

Turn Frame Job on there, adding it with **+** if it isn't listed, and press **Record** again. No relaunch is needed.

## Camera

If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears. It reads "Frame Job records the camera you choose, into a file of its own. Nothing is sent anywhere."

- **Allow** carries on to the microphone check and the countdown.
- **Don't Allow** leaves the panel idle, with a note saying the camera isn't granted.

If you've denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Camera pane instead, and the note says so. Turn it on there and relaunch Frame Job.

## Microphone

If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears. It reads "Frame Job records the microphone you choose alongside a screen recording, into a file of its own beside the movie. Nothing is sent anywhere."

- **Allow** starts the countdown straight away, as long as the panel is still open.
- **Don't Allow** leaves the panel idle, with a note saying the microphone isn't granted.

If you've denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Microphone pane instead, and the note says so. Turn it on there and relaunch Frame Job.

## If you started Frame Job from a terminal

A Frame Job started from a terminal or another app runs under that app's permissions, not its own. Turning on Frame Job in System Settings then makes no difference.

The panel's note says so, and names the process that launched it by its pid:

> This Frame Job was launched by another process (pid 4182), so the grant that counts is that application's — the terminal's, for a shell launch; or relaunch with open -a "Frame Job".

Either give the permission to that app, or quit Frame Job and start it from the Finder, the Dock or `open -a "Frame Job"`.

In a launch like this, Frame Job doesn't remember having asked. Each press without Screen Recording shows the prompt again rather than opening System Settings.

## The panel steps aside

The recorder panel usually floats above other windows. While a macOS prompt or System Settings is up, it stops floating so that it doesn't cover them. It floats again on your next press of **Record**, or when you open the panel again.

## macOS's recurring alert

macOS periodically asks whether to keep letting Frame Job record the screen. Frame Job can't see this alert, and the permission still reads as granted, so a capture waiting behind it looks like a recording that won't start.

If the panel stays on **Starting…** and then says "The recording did not start within 20 s.", look for the alert on the screen. Answer it and press **Record** again.

## With an agent

`record_screen` never asks for a permission and never opens System Settings, because a prompt needs a person in front of it. It reads each permission it needs and, if one is missing, stops with the same sentence, naming the pane. Grant it once from the panel.

If the recording doesn't start or finish in time, its answer says a macOS alert may be waiting. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)
- [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/)
- [Record a camera](/recording/record-a-camera/)
- [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/)
- [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/)

---
title: "When a recording stops on its own"
description: "What Frame Job keeps when a camera, a microphone or the system stops a recording, and what to do when a recording can't be added."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A recording can lose a device or end without you pressing Stop. Frame Job keeps what it captured, and tells you what happened. This page says what lands in each case, and what to do about what doesn't.

<AtAGlance
  where={["The recorder panel's note", 'The menu-bar item']}
  tools="record_screen"
/>

## Where you'll read about it

Everything here is reported in the note on the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/). A recording that lands cleanly doesn't bring the panel back, but one with something to say does, as long as the panel was on screen when the recording began.

If the panel wasn't on screen, press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> to open it and read the note.

While a display or a window records, the panel is hidden, so the note only appears when the recording lands. While a camera on its own or a voice-over records, the panel stays up, so the note appears as it happens.

## What's kept

| What happened | Does the recording go on? | What lands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [A camera on its own stops](#a-camera-stops) | No | What was captured |
| [A camera beside the screen stops](#a-camera-stops) | Yes | The screen, and the camera up to the stop |
| [The microphone stops](#a-microphone-stops) | Yes | The picture, without that microphone file |
| [A voice-over's microphone stops](#a-voice-overs-microphone-stops) | No | What was recorded |
| [The display sleeps or goes away](#the-display-sleeps-or-the-system-stops-the-recording) | No | What was captured |
| [A stretch's movie won't read](#a-stretch-wont-read) | It has already ended | Every other stretch, and that stretch's voice if it reads |
| [A file is too short for a frame](#a-file-is-too-short-for-one-frame) | It has already ended | That file in the media list, and the rest as usual |
| [The recording can't be added](#the-recording-cant-be-added) | It has already ended | Nothing, but the files stay on disk |

## A camera stops

If a camera recording's camera stops, for example because it's unplugged, the recording ends there and what was captured lands. The note gives the reason, then "What was captured was added.":

> The camera FaceTime HD Camera stopped on its own: it was disconnected. What was captured was added.

It can also read "its session was interrupted", or give a reason from macOS.

Beside the screen, a camera that stops doesn't end the recording. The screen keeps recording, what the camera wrote up to then lands, and the note gives the same reason. Later stretches after a pause have no camera. The one exception is a camera that fails while the recording is still starting, which stops the start with that sentence.

If a camera hasn't settled at its rate when the recording begins, the recording begins anyway and the note says what it ran at:

> The camera ran at 24.0 fps, not its 30, in the 1 s it was given to settle; the recording began anyway.

## A microphone stops

A microphone that stops partway through a screen or camera recording doesn't end it. The picture keeps recording and the panel's level meter goes silent. With the panel on screen, its note says so at once:

> The microphone stopped: … The picture is still recording.

The picture lands either way. If the microphone's file didn't finish properly or won't read, it isn't added, and the note says why and where the file is, so you can [import it](/projects/import-media/) yourself. The same goes for a microphone that never started, which reads "The microphone never started recording, so the picture was recorded without it."

## A voice-over's microphone stops

A voice-over has nothing else to record, so if its microphone stops on its own, for example because it's unplugged, the voice-over ends there. What was recorded lands, with a note:

> The microphone stopped recording on its own: … The voice-over ends where it stopped.

## The display sleeps or the system stops the recording

If the display sleeps or goes away, or the system stops the recording, what was captured lands, with the note:

> The system stopped the recording (the display slept or went away); what was captured was added.

Stopping from macOS's own screen-recording indicator in the menu bar also lands the recording. The note reads "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added."

## The screen is locked

If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, no display can be shared, so a display recording can't start until one wakes. The panel's note says the display isn't shareable.

## Resume doesn't work

If **Resume Recording** fails, the recording stays paused and nothing is lost. No file is taking the picture until a resume works, so you can try again, or stop and land what you have.

The reason goes in the panel's note. During a voice-over or a camera recording it appears there at once. During a screen recording it appears when the recording lands, and the panel comes back to show it.

A **Pause Recording** that fails only beeps, because the recording is still running.

## A stretch won't read

Each stretch between pauses has its own movie. If one won't read, for example an empty file from a pause right after a resume, it's left out, and the stretches that do read land. The note names the file and everything it left on disk:

> A segment was left out. … Its files are kept at …

Only a recording with no readable movie at all fails, and its note names every file.

### Its voice still lands

If a left-out stretch's microphone file reads, it lands without its picture, on the Microphone track in the slot the picture would have had. The picture track keeps a gap there, and the next picture starts after it. The note reads "The left-out segment's microphone, …, was added to the project without its picture."

That stretch's camera file stays on disk and the note names it, but it isn't added.

In a new project, a left-out voice from before the first picture has no timeline to sit on, so it lands in the media list without a clip, and the note says so.

## A file is too short for one frame

A file too short for one frame can't become a clip. It lands in the media list, the rest of the recording lands as usual, and the note says so:

> … is too short for a frame (12 ms) and was added to the media list without a clip.

## The recording can't be added

If a recording can't be added, nothing goes on the timeline, but the files are safe. The note names every one, so you can [import them](/projects/import-media/):

> The recording was saved at … but could not be added: …

These are the usual reasons:

| What happened | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The project is at its limit of 64 tracks and the recording needs a new one. If the picture would fit but the microphone wouldn't, none of it is added. | [Delete a track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) you don't need, then import the files. |
| You were still dragging on the timeline. Frame Job waits for a drag to end, for up to 20 s. | Import the files. |

If the files don't finish writing within 10 s of Stop, the note reads "The recording did not finish writing within 10 s." and names the files kept on disk.

## Very long recordings

A recording longer than 9:59:59 carries on as usual, but the menu-bar item's label gets wider than the item was sized for.

## With an agent

`record_screen` reports all of this in its answer, so an agent can tell what stopped and what landed. With the screen locked, it stops before recording and says that no display is shareable. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/)
- [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/)
- [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/)
- [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/)
- [The menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.
